evidence_limitations: The main figures strongly support complex membership and HSP90 dependence, but the absent online Expanded Methods prevent verification of the HSP90 siRNA and antibody identities and therefore leave alpha-versus-beta scope unresolved. RIPK3 re-expression is a pathway rescue, not purified folding proof.
claim_summary: Sequential purification and mass spectrometry of tagged RIPK3 recovered HSP90 and p23, coimmunoprecipitation placed RIPK3 in an HSP90-p23-RIPK1 complex, 17-AAG or p23 depletion blocked RIPK3 and MLKL phosphorylation and necroptosis, and HSP90 knockdown reduced RIPK3 abundance and activation. Re-expression of RIPK3 rescued much of the HSP90-knockdown phenotype, supporting an HSP90-p23-dependent RIPK3 client/activation mechanism.

source.title: Stomatin-Mediated Inhibition of the Akt Signaling Axis Suppresses Tumor Growth.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Human LNCaP, HepG2, and 22Rv1 cancer cells with inducible stomatin, stomatin or HSP90 siRNA, endogenous and tagged-protein coimmunoprecipitation, GST-stomatin pull-down, PDPK1 deletion mapping, Akt signaling, and tumor-model context.
evidence_limitations: The paper does not distinguish HSP90AA1 from HSP90AB1 or directly reconstitute purified HSP90-PDPK1 binding. Supplementary Table S1 and supporting Figures S4-S5 are absent, preventing independent review of antibody and knockdown-control details.
claim_summary: HSP90 knockdown reduced PDPK1 protein and Akt phosphorylation, endogenous PDPK1 coimmunoprecipitated with HSP90, and stomatin overexpression reduced whereas stomatin knockdown increased the PDPK1-HSP90 association. Stomatin bound the N-terminal PDPK1 region that contains the mapped HSP90-binding domain and competitively disrupted HSP90 association, while unchanged PDPK1 mRNA supported post-transcriptional protein maintenance.

source.title: Targeting the Extracellular HSP90 Co-Chaperone Morgana Inhibits Cancer Cell Migration and Promotes Anticancer Immunity.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AA1/Hsp90alpha; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Human MDA-MB-231 and BT549 breast-cancer cells with conditioned-medium analysis, HSP90AA1 knockdown, Morgana-HSP90 extracellular coimmunoprecipitation, recombinant Morgana rescue, extracellular HSP90 neutralization, LRP1 knockdown, LRP1-cluster-II pull-down, and migration assays.
evidence_limitations: The current paper proves joint extracellular HSP90 and LRP1 dependence for Morgana-driven migration but does not directly show an HSP90-LRP1 complex or purified pairwise binding. HSP90AA1 is identified as the main secreted isoform, yet the decisive functional blocking antibody is labeled only HSP90; alpha assignment therefore applies to the extracellular pool and not a directly isoform-resolved ternary complex.
claim_summary: Extracellular recombinant Morgana restored migration of Morgana-depleted breast-cancer cells, and that rescue was independently abolished by an extracellular HSP90-blocking antibody and by LRP1 depletion. Morgana bound recombinant LRP1 cluster II only in cancer-cell conditioned medium, consistent with an additional extracellular mediator. The authors nominate HSP90 as that mediator because it binds Morgana and is already known to bind LRP1, but explicitly state that the proposed ternary bridge remains unproven.

source.title: HSP90 drives the Rab11a-mediated vesicular transport of the cell surface receptors in osteoclasts.

isoform_scope_note: Both cytosolic HSP90 isoforms were measured in the reported experiment; measurement alone does not establish isoform exclusivity.
model_context: Mouse RAW-D osteoclast precursors and RANKL-differentiated osteoclasts, with endogenous and GFP-Rab11a, isoform-specific HSP90 immunoprecipitation and microscopy, 17-AAG perturbation, Rab11a gain/loss experiments, and receptor/lysosomal trafficking readouts.
evidence_limitations: The study does not establish purified pairwise binding, distinguish whether Rab11a contacts HSP90 directly, or show HSP90-dependent Rab11a turnover. Its authors explicitly note that direct versus indirect binding remains unresolved, and the inhibitor leaves Rab11a abundance unchanged.
claim_summary: Reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation detected Rab11a in complexes with both HSP90alpha and HSP90beta specifically in differentiated RAW-D-derived osteoclasts, and microscopy placed Rab11a with both isoforms in endosomal compartments. 17-AAG disrupted both associations and altered Rab11a-dependent receptor and lysosomal trafficking, but it did not reduce Rab11a abundance; the current source therefore supports an alpha/beta HSP90 complex and trafficking relationship rather than a canonical stability-client call.

source.title: HSP70 attenuates neuronal necroptosis through the HSP90alpha-RIPK3 pathway following neuronal trauma.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Primary embryonic rat cortical neurons exposed to scratch injury plus glutamate, with HSP70 inhibition or activation, geldanamycin perturbation, immunoblotting and immunostaining of HSP90alpha/RIPK3/MLKL, and necrotic-cell readouts.
evidence_limitations: The HSP90 intervention is geldanamycin, not an HSP90AA1-selective reagent; no HSP90-RIPK3 co-IP, purified binding, isoform-specific genetic perturbation, stability/degradation experiment, or alpha-versus-beta comparison is reported. RIPK3 client status is prior-literature background rather than a result retested here.
claim_summary: In a primary rat cortical-neuron trauma model, injury increased HSP90alpha abundance, HSP70 inhibition further increased HSP90alpha together with total and phosphorylated RIPK3 and MLKL, and geldanamycin reduced RIPK3/MLKL abundance and phosphorylation together with necrotic death. These experiments support broad cytosolic HSP90-dependent regulation of the RIPK3 necroptosis pathway, but not an alpha-resolved RIPK3 client relationship.

source.title: The HSP90 Inhibitor Pimitespib Targets Regulatory T Cells in the Tumor Microenvironment.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Human PBMC and MJ T-cell experiments, HEK293 cells expressing exogenous FOXP3, paired human gastric-cancer trial biopsies, and syngeneic mouse tumor models, with pimitespib treatment, FOXP3 RNA/protein and regulatory-T-cell phenotyping, STAT5 pathway interrogation, and immune/tumor-response readouts.
evidence_limitations: The source does not show HSP90-FOXP3 binding, FOXP3 stability dependence, or an individual HSP90 isoform relationship. The strongest STAT5B epistasis, rescue, and HSP90-STAT5 association panels are in a missing supplement, so the indirect mechanism cannot be independently figure-checked locally.
claim_summary: Pimitespib reduced FOXP3-high effector regulatory T cells across cultured human immune cells, human gastric-cancer trial specimens, and mouse tumors, and decreased FOXP3 RNA and protein in the MJ T-cell line. Exogenous FOXP3 in HEK293 cells was unaffected, while the manuscript places reduced STAT5 phosphorylation and the supplementary STAT5B knockdown/rescue experiments between HSP90 inhibition and FOXP3 loss; this supports FOXP3 as an indirect downstream regulated target, not an HSP90 client.

source.title: The HSP90 Inhibitor Pimitespib Targets Regulatory T Cells in the Tumor Microenvironment.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
evidence_limitations: The measured physical pair is HSP90–STAT5, not HSP90AA1–FOXP3; pimitespib is not an alpha-selective pair assay. Publisher Figure S3: https://ndownloader.figshare.com/files/65623991
claim_summary: In MJ cells, generic HSP90 coimmunoprecipitates with STAT5; STAT5B knockdown lowers FOXP3 and STAT5B overexpression partly rescues FOXP3 expression under pimitespib.

source.title: PRMT5-mediated arginine methylation of HSP90AA1 drives esophageal squamous cell carcinoma progression.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AA1/Hsp90alpha; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Human 293T, TE-1, and ECA109 cell models; human ESCC tissue analyses; HSP90AA1 CRISPR knockout with wild-type or R182A rescue; PRMT5 knockdown/inhibition; CDX and PDX tumor models; and HSP90AA1 symmetric-dimethylarginine, growth, migration, invasion, EMT, and tumor-response readouts.
evidence_limitations: The locally reviewed source is exact-title bioRxiv version 1, not the final Cancer Letters article associated with PMID41966513 and journal DOI 10.1016/j.canlet.2026.218458. The result is disease-context specific, does not test HSP90AB1 as an isoform comparator, and should be checked against the final published version.
claim_summary: Reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation in 293T and esophageal squamous cell carcinoma cells linked PRMT5 with HSP90AA1, and PRMT5 knockdown or inhibition reduced HSP90AA1 symmetric dimethylarginine. HSP90AA1 R182A lost the methylation signal and, unlike wild type HSP90AA1, failed to rescue proliferation, migration, invasion, EMT markers, and xenograft growth after HSP90AA1 knockout, supporting PRMT5 as an upstream post-translational regulator of HSP90AA1.

source.title: Identification of Functional Domains of the Aryl Hydrocarbon Receptor.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Mouse AHR and ARNT synthesized in rabbit reticulocyte lysate, with TCDD treatment, anti-HSP90 immunoprecipitation, AHR deletion constructs, DNA-binding electrophoretic mobility-shift assays, dimerization assays, and cell-based CAT reporter validation.
evidence_limitations: HSP90 was assayed as an endogenous reticulocyte-lysate component rather than a purified partner, the cytosolic isoform was not identified, and no HSP90-selective perturbation or AHR abundance/folding assay establishes client dependence. The deletion effects could reflect complex architecture rather than direct contact sites.
claim_summary: Anti-HSP90 immunoprecipitation of in-vitro-translated mouse AHR showed a ligand-regulated AHR-HSP90 complex: TCDD reduced the association, and deletion mapping found that the AHR basic-helix-loop-helix and PAS-B regions each contributed to HSP90 association while deletion of the full PAS A/B region abolished it. These experiments support a strong broad-cytosolic HSP90 co-complex and domain-mapping relationship but not purified pairwise binding or isoform-resolved client dependence.

source.title: Transient interaction of Hsp90 with early unfolding intermediates of citrate synthase. Implications for heat shock in vivo.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Purified porcine-heart mitochondrial citrate synthase was heated at 43 C in vitro with Hsp90 purified from yeast or bovine pancreas, or with the E. coli Hsp90 homolog; enzyme activity, light scattering, and oxaloacetate-induced refolding were measured.
evidence_limitations: The study does not demonstrate a native cellular CS-Hsp90 complex, purified equilibrium binding, a physiologic Hsp90 requirement for citrate synthase, or HSP90AA1 versus HSP90AB1 specificity. Citrate synthase is used as a thermally unfolded model substrate, so the data support direct chaperone action without establishing a canonical in-cell client.
claim_summary: Purified yeast, bovine, and E. coli Hsp90-family proteins dose-dependently slowed thermal inactivation and suppressed aggregation of porcine citrate synthase, while oxaloacetate-triggered reactivation kinetics supported transient capture and release of structured early unfolding intermediates. The protection was ATP-independent under these cell-free heat-shock conditions.

source.title: Cdc37 is a molecular chaperone with specific functions in signal transduction.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Saccharomyces cerevisiae BJ5457 or temperature-sensitive hsp82 G170D cells expressing galactose-regulated Rous-sarcoma-virus v-Src, with anti-v-Src co-immunoprecipitation, phosphotyrosine activity readout, and high-copy CDC37 rescue.
evidence_limitations: The model uses a viral chicken kinase expressed heterologously in yeast and therefore does not establish an endogenous human SRC relationship or HSP90AA1 versus HSP90AB1 specificity. Co-immunoprecipitation establishes complex association rather than purified pairwise binding, and CDC37 rescue indicates pathway overlap rather than Hsp90 dispensability in native settings.
claim_summary: In yeast expressing oncogenic v-Src, anti-v-Src immunoprecipitation recovered both Hsp90 and Cdc37. A temperature-sensitive Hsp82 G170D allele sharply reduced v-Src-driven phosphotyrosine activity at 34 C without loss of v-Src accumulation, and Cdc37 overexpression restored that activity, supporting an Hsp90-Cdc37 client-maintenance pathway for v-Src.

source.title: Modular folding and evidence for phosphorylation-induced stabilization of an hsp90-dependent kinase.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Wild-type and Y505F p56lck were synthesized and matured in rabbit reticulocyte lysate containing endogenous Hsp90 machinery, with phosphopeptide capture, Hsp90 coadsorption/co-immunoprecipitation, geldanamycin timing, kinase assays, and native proteolytic fingerprinting.
evidence_limitations: The work is a cell-free reticulocyte-lysate model and does not resolve HSP90AA1 versus HSP90AB1. Geldanamycin is the perturbation used to infer Hsp90 function, and the proposed Y505 phosphorylation-mediated stabilization was correlated with behavior but not directly confirmed at Y505 in the lysate.
claim_summary: Rabbit-reticulocyte translation produced Hsp90-bound p56lck whose SH2 domain was folded while its catalytic domain remained Hsp90-dependent. Geldanamycin during biogenesis abolished LCK kinase activity and increased catalytic-domain protease sensitivity without preventing SH2 phosphopeptide binding; after maturation, wild-type LCK became nearly Hsp90-independent whereas the Y505F mutant retained temperature-dependent Hsp90 maintenance requirements.

source.title: Characterization of the Ah receptor-associated protein, ARA9.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Murine AHR and deletion constructs, human ARA9, and broad endogenous Hsp90 were tested in rabbit reticulocyte lysate co-immunoprecipitation and bacterial T7-tag pulldown formats; ARA9 effects on LexA-AHR ligand-response were tested in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
evidence_limitations: The original experiments define a ternary AHR-Hsp90-ARA9 complex rather than purified AHR-Hsp90 pairwise binding, do not resolve HSP90AA1 versus HSP90AB1, and do not selectively perturb Hsp90 to establish AHR folding, abundance, or stability dependence. The functional reporter result tests ARA9 addition, not Hsp90 loss.
claim_summary: In rabbit reticulocyte lysate, AHR and Hsp90 were recovered in ARA9-containing complexes, the ARA9 TPR region was necessary and sufficient to recover both proteins, and anti-Hsp90 immunoprecipitation showed that AHR selectively stabilized ARA9-Hsp90 association compared with glucocorticoid receptor. ARA9 expression also increased AHR agonist sensitivity and maximal reporter response in yeast, supporting an AHR-Hsp90-ARA9 core complex with functional signaling consequences.

source.title: Novobiocin and related coumarins and depletion of heat shock protein 90-dependent signaling proteins.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Human SKBR3 breast-cancer cells treated for 16 hours with novobiocin, chlorobiocin, coumermycin A1, etoposide, or doxorubicin, together with cellular and recombinant chicken Hsp90 affinity-binding assays.
evidence_limitations: The paper directly validates coumarin-Hsp90 binding and ERBB2 loss but does not show that ERBB2 physically associates with the assayed Hsp90 preparation, measure ERBB2 half-life or proteasomal rescue, or distinguish cytosolic HSP90AA1/HSP90AB1 from the cited ER-lumenal GRP94 relationship.
claim_summary: Novobiocin bound cellular and recombinant Hsp90 through a carboxyl-terminal region, and novobiocin, chlorobiocin, and coumermycin A1 each depleted p185ERBB2 in SKBR3 cells. Etoposide and doxorubicin did not reproduce the ERBB2 loss, and several unrelated loading or toxicity-control proteins were unchanged, supporting Hsp90-directed small-molecule depletion of ERBB2 without establishing a direct Hsp90-ERBB2 complex in this experiment.

source.title: Modulation of p53, ErbB1, ErbB2, and Raf-1 expression in lung cancer cells by depsipeptide FR901228.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Human H322 non-small-cell lung-cancer cells treated with FK228, trichostatin A, or 17-AAG for ERBB2 abundance and ERK-pathway readouts; H322 and SKBR3 cells were used for Hsp90 complex, ATP-resin, and acetylation assays centered on other clients or Hsp90 itself.
evidence_limitations: ERBB2 depletion is direct, but its link to Hsp90 acetylation is inferred from parallel experiments and analogy to p53 and Raf-1. FK228 is an HDAC inhibitor rather than a selective Hsp90 ligand, no ERBB2-Hsp90 complex is tested, and the relevant Hsp90 family member or compartment is unresolved.
claim_summary: FK228, trichostatin A, and 17-AAG depleted ERBB2 in H322 lung-cancer cells, while FK228 induced Hsp90 acetylation and reduced Hsp90 ATP-resin binding in SKBR3 cells. The paper directly showed FK228 disruption of Hsp90 complexes with mutant p53 and Raf-1, but did not assay an Hsp90-ERBB2 complex; the authors described the analogous mechanism for ERBB2 as preliminary and still under investigation.

source.title: MCEF, the newest member of the AF4 family of transcription factors involved in leukemia, is a positive transcription elongation factor-b-associated protein.

isoform_scope_note: Both cytosolic isoforms are mentioned without a necessarily resolved comparison; no specificity is inferred.
model_context: Stable FLAG-CDK9-expressing human HeLa cells, nuclear and cytoplasmic extract affinity purification across 100-500 mM KCl, vector-only controls, recombinant HSP90alpha and HSP90beta antibody calibration, protein microsequencing, and P-TEFb kinase assays.
evidence_limitations: The source establishes an HSP90-containing P-TEFb co-complex but not whether HSP90 contacts CDK9 directly, folds or stabilizes CDK9, or is required for kinase activity. Geldanamycin inhibited HIV-related readouts only at cytotoxic concentrations and therefore does not provide usable client-dependence evidence.
claim_summary: FLAG-CDK9 affinity purification from HeLa nuclear extracts recovered HSP90 at up to 500 mM KCl, Western blots detected both cytosolic Hsp90 isoforms with HSP90alpha predominant and HSP90beta low but detectable, and microsequencing independently identified HSP90 in the stringent CDK9/P-TEFb preparation. CDC37 and HSP70 were also recovered, supporting a stable CDK9-associated chaperone complex without proving direct binding or CDK9 client dependence.

source.title: Hyaluronan constitutively regulates ErbB2 phosphorylation and signaling complex formation in carcinoma cells.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Human HCT116 colon carcinoma, mouse TA3/St mammary carcinoma, and human MCF-7 mammary carcinoma cells with endogenous-hyaluronan antagonism, CD44 siRNA or soluble-CD44 expression, hyaluronan-synthesis stimulation, ErbB2 immunoprecipitation, and phosphorylation and complex-composition readouts.
evidence_limitations: Coimmunoprecipitation establishes shared complex membership but not a direct Hsp90-ErbB2 interface. Hsp90 itself was shown in the hyaluronan-oligomer experiment, whereas several orthogonal perturbations measured Cdc37 rather than Hsp90; neither Hsp90 isoform, Hsp90 dependence, ErbB2 turnover, nor rescue was tested.
claim_summary: Endogenous ErbB2 immunoprecipitates from HCT116 and TA3/St carcinoma cells contained Hsp90 and Cdc37. Hyaluronan oligomers markedly reduced Hsp90, Cdc37, activated ErbB2, CD44, ezrin, and PI3K-p110 in the complex without reducing total ErbB2, and the complex changes were replicated and quantified; CD44 antagonism or depletion independently reduced Cdc37-containing complex assembly. These data support Hsp90 as a member of a regulated ErbB2 signaling complex but do not establish direct pairwise binding or current-source client stability.

source.title: Human leukemias with mutated FLT3 kinase are synergistically sensitive to FLT3 and Hsp90 inhibitors: the key role of the STAT5 signal transduction pathway.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Sixteen human leukemia cell lines for drug-sensitivity profiling, with mechanistic time courses in MV4;11 ITD-FLT3, SEMK2-M1 amplified wild-type FLT3, and RS4;11 non-amplified wild-type FLT3 cells; FLT3 siRNA, 17-AAG, GTP14564, phosphorylation, proliferation, cell-cycle, and apoptosis readouts.
evidence_limitations: 17-AAG pharmacology does not identify HSP90AA1 versus HSP90AB1 and cannot by itself prove direct binding or definitive client status. No Hsp90 knockdown, isoform-specific perturbation, Hsp90-FLT3 coimmunoprecipitation, turnover measurement, proteasome rescue, or purified interaction was performed in this source.
claim_summary: The Hsp90 inhibitor 17-AAG reduced total FLT3 and AKT across time-course experiments and reduced phosphorylated FLT3 in ITD-FLT3 MV4;11 and amplified-wild-type FLT3 SEMK2-M1 cells, while inducing Hsp70. Across 16 leukemia lines, sensitivity to 17-AAG and the FLT3 inhibitor GTP14564 tracked FLT3 mutation or amplification, and the two agents synergized in FLT3-dependent lines. The current paper therefore supports pharmacologic Hsp90-dependent regulation of FLT3 abundance and signaling, but its statement that FLT3 is an Hsp90 client comes from prior work and is not re-established by physical or genetic Hsp90 assays here.

source.title: Mass spectrometry identification of NASP binding partners in HeLa cells.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AB1/Hsp90beta; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Human HeLa very-high-molecular-weight nuclear extract subjected to reversible DTSSP crosslinking, two-dimensional gel separation, MALDI-TOF and MALDI-TOF/TOF; anti-NASP affinity purification from separate HeLa nuclear and cytoplasmic fractions assessed sNASP, tNASP, and HSP90 by Western blot.
evidence_limitations: Crosslinking and affinity copurification do not establish a direct NASP-HSP90 interface, stoichiometry, or functional dependency. The beta assignment is sequence based; the validation antibody was broad HSP90, no alpha comparator was tested, and no NASP or HSP90 perturbation assessed biological function.
claim_summary: Reversible crosslinking of a very-high-molecular-weight HeLa nuclear fraction followed by two-dimensional separation and MALDI-TOF identified HSP90 as the most abundant recovered NASP-associated protein, with 20 matched peptides and two tandem-MS-confirmed sequences. The reported AAH04928/BC004928 sequence and beta-specific peptide NPDDITQEEYGEFYK resolve the mass-spectrometry identification to HSP90AB1, and anti-NASP affinity purification independently showed HSP90 copurifying with both sNASP and tNASP from nuclear and cytoplasmic fractions. These experiments establish robust shared-complex association, not purified pairwise binding.

source.title: Synergism between etoposide and 17-AAG in leukemia cells: critical roles for Hsp90, FLT3, topoisomerase II, Chk1, and Rad51.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Human leukemia cell lines with ITD-FLT3, wild-type FLT3, or no detectable FLT3, including MV4;11, Molm13, RS4;11, and HPB-Null, treated with 17-AAG, etoposide, FLT ligand, or FLT3 siRNA.
evidence_limitations: The current source does not assay an Hsp90-FLT3 complex, direct binding, turnover kinetics, rescue by either cytosolic isoform, or isoform-selective perturbation. Much of the functional evidence is generated in combination-treatment and FLT3-pathway contexts.
claim_summary: 17-AAG reduced total and phosphorylated FLT3 together with AKT, Chk1, and RAD51 in leukemia cells, and FLT3 knockdown reproduced loss of downstream AKT, Chk1, and RAD51 signaling while leaving Hsp90 abundance unchanged. These experiments support Hsp90-inhibitor dependence of wild-type and ITD-FLT3 signaling and a candidate-client interpretation, but the paper cites rather than directly retests the prior Hsp90-FLT3 client relationship.

source.title: Synergism between etoposide and 17-AAG in leukemia cells: critical roles for Hsp90, FLT3, topoisomerase II, Chk1, and Rad51.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Human leukemia cell lines with ITD-FLT3, wild-type FLT3, or no detectable FLT3, treated with 17-AAG, etoposide, FLT ligand, or FLT3 siRNA, with RAD51 protein and DNA-damage and apoptosis readouts.
evidence_limitations: The study does not assay Hsp90-RAD51 binding, a shared complex, RAD51 folding or turnover, Hsp90 genetic dependence, or either cytosolic isoform. RAD51 loss is also produced by FLT3 knockdown, making an indirect pathway explanation more appropriate than client status.
claim_summary: 17-AAG reduced RAD51 abundance in leukemia cells and enhanced etoposide-associated DNA damage and apoptosis, but FLT3 knockdown also lowered RAD51. The current results therefore place RAD51 within an Hsp90-inhibitor-sensitive FLT3 and DNA-repair response rather than establishing RAD51 as a direct Hsp90 partner or client.

source.title: Inhibition of the heat shock protein 90 molecular chaperone in vitro and in vivo by novel, synthetic, potent resorcinylic pyrazole/isoxazole amide analogues.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Human SKMEL2 and WM266.4 melanoma and BT20 breast carcinoma cells exposed to VER-49009 or VER-50589, with purified Hsp90 compound-binding and ATPase assays and HSP90alpha nucleotide-binding-domain crystallography used to validate the inhibitor mechanism.
evidence_limitations: The current paper does not demonstrate Hsp90-PRMT5 binding, co-complex membership, PRMT5 turnover kinetics, rescue, or isoform-specific cellular dependence. The HSP90alpha structural experiment validates compound engagement but does not resolve the isoform responsible for PRMT5 depletion. The cited antibody list and Supplementary Figure S1 are absent locally.
claim_summary: Two chemically related resorcinylic Hsp90 inhibitors, VER-49009 and VER-50589, depleted PRMT5 over time in SKMEL2 melanoma cells, and VER-50589 also depleted PRMT5 in BT20 breast cells. Compound-target engagement was supported by Hsp90 binding, ATPase, and HSP90alpha nucleotide-binding-domain structural assays, but prior HSP90-PRMT5 binding and potential-client status were cited rather than directly retested. The source supports inhibitor-sensitive PRMT5 abundance and candidate-client direction, not a current direct interaction.

source.title: Prohibitin regulates TGF-beta induced apoptosis as a downstream effector of Smad-dependent and -independent signaling.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AB1/Hsp90beta; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Human PC-3 prostate-cancer cells treated with TGF-beta; whole-cell lysates were immunoprecipitated with anti-PHB, differential SDS-PAGE bands were excised, and proteins were identified by LC-MS/MS and Mascot.
evidence_limitations: Main Table II provides the exact beta accession but not HSP90 peptide counts, sequence coverage, enrichment magnitude, untreated comparison, or a reciprocal/orthogonal interaction test. PHB is primarily analyzed as a TGF-beta/MAPK/mitochondrial-apoptosis effector, and the HSP90 hit is not followed mechanistically.
claim_summary: Anti-PHB immunoprecipitation from TGF-beta-treated human PC-3 prostate-cancer cells followed by LC-MS/MS identified heat-shock protein HSP90 beta, accession P08238, among the potential PHB binding partners in main Table II. This is current, beta-resolved affinity-capture evidence for association with a PHB-containing complex, but the paper does not validate the HSP90AB1 hit by reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation, direct binding, or HSP90 perturbation and does not interpret PHB as an HSP90 client.

source.title: A direct role for Hsp90 in pre-RISC formation in Drosophila.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Drosophila melanogaster S2 cells and lysates expressing Flag-Ago2 or Flag-Dicer2 were used for siRNA processing, unwinding, RISC-formation, slicer, siRNA-protein cross-linking, northern-blot, and co-immunoprecipitation assays.
evidence_limitations: The main functional data are pharmacologic and non-human; there is no Hsp90 genetic depletion/rescue, purified pairwise binding, or human HSP90AA1-versus-HSP90AB1 comparison. The co-immunoprecipitation, radicicol confirmation, dose response, and Ago2-stability control are described in the text but their Supplemental Figure 1 panels are absent from the archive.
claim_summary: In Drosophila S2-cell lysates, geldanamycin blocked siRNA-duplex unwinding, RISC formation, and siRNA loading onto Ago2 without impairing Dicer2 processing, RLC formation, Ago2 slicer activity after RISC assembly, or Ago2 stability. The text further reports radicicol replication and Hsp90 recovery in an Ago2 immunoprecipitate in Supplemental Figure 1. These data support a conserved broad-Hsp90 candidate-client relationship in which Hsp90 activity makes Ago2 competent to receive siRNA, but they do not resolve a human cytosolic isoform.

source.title: A switch from hBrm to Brg1 at IFNγ-activated sequences mediates the activation of human genes.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AA1/Hsp90alpha; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Human Jurkat T-leukemia cells, Raji B-lymphoma cells, and primary peripheral-blood T lymphocytes were examined under basal, 42-degree heat-shock, and interferon-gamma conditions using the HSP90AA1 promoter GAS as the principal mechanistic locus.
evidence_limitations: The source establishes promoter-level regulation and chromatin-complex switching, not physical STAT1-HSP90 protein association, HSP90-dependent STAT1 folding/stability, or a client relationship. IFN-gamma responses are cell-type specific, while the strongest HSP90AA1 evidence is the Jurkat heat-shock model; HSP90AB1 is mentioned as prior work rather than tested as the principal current locus.
claim_summary: At the human HSP90AA1/hsp90alpha promoter, endogenous STAT1 occupies the gamma-activated-sequence element under basal and heat-shock conditions. Native STAT1 recruits hBrm and an mSin3/HDAC repressor complex, whereas heat-shock-induced STAT1 phosphorylation and hBrm acetylation favor Brg1 recruitment and HSP90AA1 transcriptional activation. ChIP, promoter mutation, RNAi, reporter, co-IP, and phosphorylation-mutant experiments support STAT1 as an upstream transcriptional regulator of HSP90AA1, not as an Hsp90 client or protein-binding partner.

source.title: A specific function for the histone chaperone NASP to fine-tune a reservoir of soluble H3-H4 in the histone supply chain.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AB1/Hsp90beta; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Human HeLa S3, U-2 OS, and HEK293 cells with NASP, HSP90AB1/HSP90 beta, HSP90 alpha, Hsc70, and LAMP2A siRNA perturbations; readouts focused on soluble and chromatin-associated histone H3-H4 pools.
evidence_limitations: The decisive relationship is genetic/functional rather than physical: the article does not assay an NASP-HSP90 complex, and its NASP affinity experiments do not display HSP90. HSP90 beta acts in a broader Hsc70/LAMP2A chaperone-mediated-autophagy model. The alpha negative result is text-only, and missing Supplemental Figure S6 contains specificity and fractionation controls relevant to the proposed mechanism.
claim_summary: In human cells, NASP depletion reduced the soluble H3-H4 reservoir. Figure 6C shows that isoform-specific depletion of HSP90AB1/HSP90 beta, using an siRNA directed to NM_007355.2, rescued soluble H3-H4 loss caused by NASP depletion; Hsc70 depletion produced a related rescue, and LAMP2A experiments implicated chaperone-mediated autophagy. The authors report that HSP90 alpha depletion did not increase soluble histones, although that negative result is not shown. These current data support beta-resolved functional epistasis in a NASP-histone-quality-control pathway, but do not demonstrate NASP-HSP90 binding, co-complex membership, or client status.

source.title: A role for Fkbp6 and the chaperone machinery in piRNA amplification and transposon silencing.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Mouse Fkbp6-null testes and testis extract, HEK293T cells expressing mouse HA-Fkbp6 and Fkbp6 TPR mutants, purified Bombyx mori Shutdown and BmHsp90 proteins, and Bombyx BmN4 cells treated with geldanamycin for Ago3/piRNA assays.
evidence_limitations: The mammalian interaction assays do not resolve HSP90AA1 versus HSP90AB1 and do not demonstrate purified direct binding. Direct biochemical binding and inhibitor-dependent piRNA effects are shown in the Bombyx ortholog system, and the authors caution that the precise mammalian mechanism may differ. The evidence supports cochaperone/complementary chaperone-complex semantics, not an HSP90 client assignment.
claim_summary: Figure 3 shows that mouse Fkbp6 associates with Hsp90 in mouse testis extract and that expressed mouse HA-Fkbp6 co-precipitates endogenous Hsp90 in HEK293T cells. TPR-domain mapping and the Fkbp6 K254A mutation support a specific cochaperone-like interaction. Purified direct binding was demonstrated for the Bombyx mori Shutdown ortholog with BmHsp90, while geldanamycin experiments in Bombyx BmN4 cells linked Hsp90 activity to Ago3-associated piRNA processing. The mammalian data support an unresolved-cytosolic-Hsp90 FKBP6 cochaperone complex, not client status; the purified and pharmacologic mechanistic extensions are species-ortholog context.

source.title: Protein kinase D2 and heat shock protein 90 beta are required for BCL6-associated zinc finger protein mRNA stabilization induced by vascular endothelial growth factor-A.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AB1/Hsp90beta; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Human umbilical-vein endothelial cells stimulated with VEGF-A or PMA, with PRKD-family siRNA, wild-type, constitutively active, or kinase-dead PRKD2, BAZF/BCL6B RNA half-life and 3-prime-UTR reporters, HSP90AB1-resolved RNA pull-down mass spectrometry and RNA immunoprecipitation, and Pu-H71 or 17-AAG treatment.
evidence_limitations: PRKD2 is positioned upstream by genetic and reporter experiments, but no PRKD2-HSP90AB1 complex or direct phosphorylation is demonstrated. The HSP90 inhibitors are not beta-selective, although HSP90AB1 identity is independently resolved by mass spectrometry and an HSP90beta antibody in the RNA-association assays. The RNA target is BAZF/BCL6B, not BCL6.
claim_summary: PRKD2 knockdown, constitutively active and kinase-dead mutants, and 3-prime-UTR reporters established PRKD2-dependent stabilization of BAZF/BCL6B mRNA after VEGF-A signaling. Biotinylated BAZF RNA pull-down and mass spectrometry identified HSP90AB1, anti-HSP90beta RNA immunoprecipitation showed VEGF-A-dependent BAZF RNA enrichment, and HSP90 inhibitors shortened BAZF RNA half-life and suppressed PRKD2-dependent reporter activity. PRKD2 did not measurably phosphorylate HSP90beta, supporting an indirect upstream regulatory relationship rather than direct PRKD2-HSP90beta binding.

source.title: Ca2+/S100 proteins inhibit the interaction of FKBP38 with Bcl-2 and Hsp90.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Purified recombinant S100-family proteins, human FKBP38 fragments and mutants, recombinant Hsp90, and Bcl-2 in Ca2+-dependent pull-down and surface-plasmon-resonance assays, with limited Huh-7 and SH-SY5Y cellular validation for other S100-family members.
evidence_limitations: The Hsp90 construct is not resolved to HSP90AA1 versus HSP90AB1. S100A1-specific regulation of the FKBP38-Hsp90 interaction is demonstrated in cell-free assays; cellular complex and stability experiments use endogenous S100A2/S100A6 or overexpressed active S100P rather than S100A1. Competition at FKBP38 does not establish direct S100A1-Hsp90 contact.
claim_summary: Purified S100A1 bound directly and with high affinity to the FKBP38 TPR and adjacent calmodulin-binding region, and increasing Ca2+-bound S100A1 dose-dependently displaced recombinant Hsp90 from FKBP38 in pull-down assays. Surface plasmon resonance and FKBP38 deletion and carboxylate-clamp mutants mapped overlapping S100A1- and Hsp90-sensitive FKBP38 regions. The source supports S100A1 as a direct FKBP38-binding regulator of FKBP38-Hsp90 complex assembly, not as a direct Hsp90-binding partner or client.

source.title: The HIV protease inhibitor nelfinavir down-regulates RET signaling and induces apoptosis in medullary thyroid cancer cells.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Human TT and MZ-CRC-1 medullary-thyroid-cancer cell lines with endogenous RET C634W and RET M918T, respectively, were exposed to clinically reachable nelfinavir concentrations; a 36-case human MTC tissue microarray supplied HSP90-expression context.
evidence_limitations: Nelfinavir has pleiotropic protease-inhibitor, oxidative-stress, lipid-raft, and proposed mitochondrial-HSP90 effects, so RET loss cannot be assigned exclusively to cytosolic HSP90 inhibition. The paper does not resolve HSP90AA1 versus HSP90AB1 or test direct complex formation. Supplemental Table 1, absent locally, is claim-bearing for the protein-versus-transcript distinction.
claim_summary: In human TT and MZ-CRC-1 medullary-thyroid-cancer cells carrying endogenous C634W or M918T RET, nelfinavir reduced RET protein and downstream pERK while total HSP90 abundance remained unchanged and established HSP90-client controls also fell. The main article therefore supplies current broad-HSP90 pharmacologic evidence consistent with mutant RET being an HSP90 candidate client, but it does not show RET-HSP90 co-immunoprecipitation, purified binding, HSP90 genetic perturbation, or isoform specificity. The asserted absence of a RET-mRNA change is supported only by missing Supplemental Table 1.

source.title: Changes in PTTG1 by human TERT gene expression modulate the self-renewal of placenta-derived mesenchymal stem cells.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Primary human placental mesenchymal stem cells and hTERT-transfected immortalized derivatives were compared under control or PTTG1-siRNA conditions; TERT- and Ku70-directed immunoprecipitations tested the self-renewal-associated complex.
evidence_limitations: The HSP90 antibody is reported generically and no HSP90AA1/HSP90AB1 comparison is made. The study does not immunoprecipitate HSP90 reciprocally, test purified TERT-HSP90 binding, or perturb HSP90 to establish that TERT folding, activity, or stability depends on the chaperone. TERT overexpression and aneuploid immortalized cells limit generalization.
claim_summary: Anti-TERT immunoprecipitation from human placenta-derived mesenchymal stem cells recovered HSP90 together with PTTG1 and Ku70, and anti-Ku70 immunoprecipitation recovered both TERT and HSP90. Figure 6 shows that the HSP90-containing association persists across naive and TERT-transfected cells and after PTTG1 knockdown. This is current broad-HSP90 complex evidence for TERT, but not purified pairwise binding, an HSP90-perturbation experiment, client dependence, or alpha/beta resolution.

source.title: ATM kinase sustains HER2 tumorigenicity in breast cancer.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Human HER2-overexpressing MCF7, SKBR3, BT474, and SKOV3 models, HEK293 transfection context, MCF7-HER2 xenografts, NeuT transgenic mice, and a retrospective human breast-cancer cohort were used to connect ATM activity to HER2 stability and tumorigenicity.
evidence_limitations: HSP90 is not isoform-resolved and ATM is not tested as an HSP90 client or purified binding partner. Main Figure 4 establishes regulation of HER2-HSP90 association, not physical ATM-HSP90 contact. The direct ternary-complex evidence is confined to absent Supplementary Figure 7B-C, and KU-55933 pharmacology is supplemented, but not replaced, by ATM RNA interference.
claim_summary: ATM knockdown or kinase inhibition reduced HSP90 recovered with immunoprecipitated HER2 in MCF7-HER2 and SKBR3 cells, with the authors normalizing the co-immunoprecipitation to HER2 protein. The same perturbations increased HER2 ubiquitination and accelerated HER2 loss, establishing ATM as an upstream regulator of the HER2-HSP90 chaperone complex. The main article does not show an ATM-HSP90 pairwise interaction; its ternary HER2-HSP90-ATM complex claim is assigned to missing Supplementary Figure 7B-C.

source.title: ATM kinase sustains HER2 tumorigenicity in breast cancer.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
evidence_limitations: The retrieved supplement labels the antibody and bands HSP90 without beta identity. Co-recovery in a HER2 complex and ATM-dependent HSP90 recruitment do not establish direct ATM-HSP90AB1 binding.
claim_summary: ATM knockdown or kinase inhibition reduces pan-HSP90 recovered with HER2; Supplementary Figure 7C shows ATM and pan-HSP90 in HER2 immunoprecipitates.

source.title: Blocking HSP90 Addiction Inhibits Tumor Cell Proliferation, Metastasis Development, and Synergistically Acts with Zoledronic Acid to Delay Osteosarcoma Progression.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Human HOS-MNNG osteosarcoma cells and intratibial HOS-MNNG xenografts in nude mice were treated with PF4942847, with gelatin zymography, immunoblotting, migration/invasion assays, lung histology, and tumor phenotyping.
evidence_limitations: The paper does not test MMP9-HSP90 co-immunoprecipitation, purified binding, MMP9 stability after genetic HSP90 perturbation, or cytosolic isoform specificity. Unchanged MMP9 mRNA and in-vivo MMP9 immunostaining are assigned to missing Supplementary Figures S2A and S3, so the strongest complete main-article evidence is drug-linked activity and protein loss in one osteosarcoma model.
claim_summary: The synthetic HSP90 inhibitor PF4942847 reduced MMP9 gelatinase activity and MMP9 protein in HOS-MNNG osteosarcoma cells while suppressing migration, invasion, angiogenesis, and pulmonary metastases. The current results therefore support MMP9 as a downstream HSP90-regulated effector in this pharmacologic osteosarcoma context, not as a demonstrated HSP90 client or physical binding partner.

source.title: Blocking HSP90 Addiction Inhibits Tumor Cell Proliferation, Metastasis Development, and Synergistically Acts with Zoledronic Acid to Delay Osteosarcoma Progression.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Human HOS-MNNG and U2OS osteosarcoma cells were exposed to PF4942847 alone or with zoledronic acid, with c-RAF1 protein assessed alongside AKT, ERK, and c-MET pathway components.
evidence_limitations: Only drug-associated c-RAF1 protein loss is shown for the exact route. The paper lacks HSP90 genetic depletion/rescue, reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation, purified binding, RAF1 turnover kinetics, and alpha/beta resolution. Broader transcript and proteasome-rescue controls are supplemental and are not visibly tied to c-RAF1 in the recovered main article.
claim_summary: PF4942847 reduced c-RAF1 protein in osteosarcoma cells, including in the zoledronic-acid combination experiment, and the paper interprets the drug response within depletion of HSP90 client proteins. This is current inhibitor-linked protein-abundance evidence consistent with RAF1 being a candidate HSP90 client, but the source does not test RAF1-HSP90 association, RAF1 transcript abundance, proteasome rescue specifically for RAF1, or individual HSP90 isoforms.

source.title: AR-12 Inhibits Multiple Chaperones Concomitant With Stimulating Autophagosome Formation Collectively Preventing Virus Replication.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Human patient-derived GBM5 and GBM12 glioblastoma models were treated with OSU-03012/AR-12; pairwise immunofluorescence and HSP90 immunoprecipitation assessed AhA1 association, with separate tagged-HSP90 ATPase experiments establishing drug action on the chaperone.
evidence_limitations: The HSP90 reagents and figure labels are not alpha/beta-resolved, the co-immunoprecipitation is not a purified direct-binding assay, and AhA1 is not reciprocally immunoprecipitated. The work is embedded in broad chaperone pharmacology and glioblastoma models rather than an isoform-specific cochaperone study.
claim_summary: In GBM5 cells, HSP90 and AhA1 co-localized under vehicle conditions and their merged signal was disrupted by OSU-03012. In GBM12 lysates, HSP90 immunoprecipitation recovered AhA1 and the association decreased after drug exposure. These current experiments support AHSA1 as a broad-HSP90 cochaperone/complex partner, but the manuscript's generic HSP90 labels do not validate the BioGRID route's HSP90AA1 specificity.

source.title: AR-12 Inhibits Multiple Chaperones Concomitant With Stimulating Autophagosome Formation Collectively Preventing Virus Replication.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Human GBM5 and GBM12 glioblastoma models treated with OSU-03012/AR-12; multiple HSP27 antibodies were documented, and HSP90-HSP27 association was examined by pairwise microscopy and HSP90 immunoprecipitation.
evidence_limitations: The HSP90 reagent is generic, HSP27 is not reciprocally immunoprecipitated, and drug-induced loss of both abundance and association complicates separation of complex disruption from protein depletion. The assay does not establish purified direct binding, client dependence, or alpha-specific interaction.
claim_summary: The paper uses the standard HSP27 protein label for HSPB1. Main Figure 3 shows HSP90-HSP27 co-localization and HSP27 recovery after HSP90 immunoprecipitation, with OSU-03012 disrupting the association; it also documents reduced HSP27 abundance after drug exposure. This is current broad-HSP90 complex evidence for HSPB1, but the manuscript does not resolve HSP90AA1 from HSP90AB1 or demonstrate purified direct binding.

source.title: The evolutionary capacitor HSP90 buffers the regulatory effects of mammalian endogenous retroviruses.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AB1/Hsp90beta; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
evidence_limitations: The reciprocal enrichments support beta in a cellular complex, not purified direct binding or KAP1 client status. The biotin-tagged HSP90 ChIP and pan-HSP90 inhibitor do not independently resolve beta-specific chromatin action; KAP1 abundance is unchanged after inhibition.
claim_summary: In mouse embryonic stem cells, HSP90 inhibitor-resin enrichment recovers KAP1 and a band labelled HSP90beta, while KAP1 immunoprecipitation recovers an HSP90beta band. Online Methods identify the detection antibody as Abcam ab53497, marketed and knockout-validated for HSP90beta. Supplementary Figure 6 shows HSP90 chromatin occupancy and KAP1/H3K9me3 changes after HSP90 inhibition.

source.title: HSP90 Shapes the Consequences of Human Genetic Variation.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AB1/Hsp90beta; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Human HEK293T cells stably expressing Rluc-HSP90AB1/HSP90 beta prey were transiently transfected with FLAG-CDC37 bait; anti-FLAG capture, luciferase co-recovery, and FLAG ELISA generated LUMIER interaction scores over 4-12 biological replicates.
evidence_limitations: The experiment is a quantitative cellular co-capture assay and does not establish purified direct binding or compare HSP90 alpha. CDC37 is included as a positive-control cochaperone, so the source supports the bounded pair and relationship class without adding a new chaperone-cycle mechanism.
claim_summary: The article's LUMIER assay used Renilla-luciferase-tagged HSP90AB1/HSP90 beta as prey and FLAG-CDC37 as a benchmark HSP90 cochaperone bait. Embedded Supplemental Figure S1A shows strong, reproducible CDC37-HSP90 binding above background across independent biological replicates. This is a beta-resolved current displayed cochaperone-pair assay, but it serves as an assay-positive control rather than a new CDC37 mechanistic investigation.

source.title: HSP90 Shapes the Consequences of Human Genetic Variation.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AB1/Hsp90beta; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Human HEK293T LUMIER and coimmunoprecipitation assays; FANCA-null patient-derived GM6914 fibroblasts reconstituted with wild-type or mutant FANCA; mitomycin-C and other genotoxic challenges; low-dose ganetespib, PU-H71, or onalespib; cycloheximide/proteasome assays; and febrile-range temperature perturbation.
evidence_limitations: The beta-resolved isoform assignment is exact for the Rluc-HSP90AB1 prey, whereas endogenous-HSP90 coimmunoprecipitation and inhibitor-dependent functional effects do not distinguish alpha from beta. Dependence varies markedly by FANCA allele, so the strongest client claim is mutation-specific rather than a uniform statement about all FANCA protein.
claim_summary: Wild-type and mutant human FANCA proteins were quantitatively tested against Rluc-HSP90AB1/HSP90 beta by LUMIER, with differential mutant engagement validated by anti-FLAG coimmunoprecipitation of endogenous HSP90. Multiple FANCA missense variants showed increased HSP90 binding; low-level HSP90 inhibitors selectively reduced mutant stability and FA-pathway function, and compensatory FANCA mutations normalized HSP90 binding, proteasomal sensitivity, and environmental dependence. The combined beta-resolved pair assays, mutation-sensitive engagement, stability, functional sensitization, and compensatory rescue support FANCA as an HSP90 client, especially for folding-compromised variants.

source.title: HSP90 Shapes the Consequences of Human Genetic Variation.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AB1/Hsp90beta; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Human HEK293T LUMIER measurements from a previously generated mutant-interactome dataset, using FLAG-tagged SOD1 variants and Rluc-HSP90AB1/HSP90 beta prey; clinical-severity comparisons focused on ALS-associated G37R and G41S alleles.
evidence_limitations: The displayed interaction is allele-specific and drawn from reanalysis of an earlier primary screen. It does not establish purified direct binding or demonstrate that HSP90 maintains SOD1 abundance or function. The result should not be generalized from G37R to wild-type SOD1 or all ALS variants.
claim_summary: The article reanalyzes a large human-mutant LUMIER dataset generated with Rluc-HSP90AB1/HSP90 beta and shows allele-specific SOD1 chaperone engagement. ALS-associated SOD1-G37R is HSP90-engaged, whereas the more severe G41S variant is HSP70-preferring. This provides beta-resolved, mutation-sensitive cellular association evidence for SOD1 but no current HSP90 perturbation, SOD1 stability, activity, or rescue assay establishing a functional client relationship.

source.title: HSP90 Shapes the Consequences of Human Genetic Variation.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AB1/Hsp90beta; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Human HEK293T LUMIER cells expressing Rluc-HSP90AB1/HSP90 beta prey and FLAG-tagged v-SRC or c-SRC baits; the constructs and interaction dataset were inherited from prior interactome work and displayed here as folding/client controls.
evidence_limitations: The strongest result is for viral oncogenic v-SRC, which is not equivalent to unmodified human SRC. The article provides no current HSP90 inhibition, SRC abundance, kinase-activity, or rescue experiment for this route, and LUMIER co-capture is not purified direct binding.
claim_summary: The LUMIER assay used Rluc-HSP90AB1/HSP90 beta as prey and compared FLAG-tagged viral oncogenic v-SRC with cellular c-SRC. Embedded Supplemental Figure S1A shows strong HSP90 engagement by v-SRC and much weaker engagement by c-SRC; the text uses v-SRC as the classical HSP90 client positive control and attributes its enhanced engagement to the oncogenic folding defect. This supports beta-resolved SRC-family client association bounded to the viral oncogenic variant, not an unrestricted claim that normal human SRC has equivalent HSP90 dependence.

source.title: G1/S phase progression is regulated by PLK1 degradation through the CDK1/beta-TrCP axis.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Human HeLa, A549, and HEK293T cells treated with geldanamycin, MG132, or CDK1 inhibitor RO-3306; CDK1 siRNA and overexpression; PLK1/beta-TrCP ubiquitination assays; synchronized-cell and flow-cytometric cell-cycle analyses.
evidence_limitations: All HSP90-linked evidence is initiated by geldanamycin, and CDK1 protein loss is observed without a direct HSP90-CDK1 complex assay. The strongest mechanistic experiments establish CDK1 as the kinase driving PLK1 degradation after HSP90 inhibition, not the molecular basis of CDK1 loss. Supplemental Figure S4 provides orthogonal CDK1-inhibitor support but is absent locally.
claim_summary: Geldanamycin treatment caused progressive loss of CDK1 protein in HeLa and A549 cells, while early CDK1 activity promoted beta-TrCP-dependent ubiquitination and degradation of misfolded PLK1 after HSP90 inhibition. CDK1 siRNA increased PLK1, CDK1 overexpression prolonged PLK1 loss after geldanamycin, and CDK1 enhanced PLK1 ubiquitination in cells and in vitro. The current article therefore places CDK1 as a pharmacologically responsive downstream kinase in an HSP90-controlled degradation pathway, but it does not assay HSP90-CDK1 binding, genetic HSP90 dependence, or isoform scope and should not by itself establish CDK1 as a direct client.

source.title: Non-canonical roles of PFKFB3 in regulation of cell cycle through binding to CDK4.

isoform_scope_note: Both cytosolic isoforms are mentioned without a necessarily resolved comparison; no specificity is inferred.
model_context: Human HEK293T, HeLa, MCF-7, and MDA-MB-231 cells were used for PFKFB3 affinity discovery, PFKFB3-CDK4 binding and mutant mapping, PFKFB3 knockdown or re-expression, CDK4 turnover and ubiquitination, and anti-Hsp90 co-immunoprecipitation; breast-cancer xenografts supplied downstream disease context.
evidence_limitations: The alpha and beta hits are listed in the discovery table without peptide counts, enrichment, or isoform-specific validation. Anti-Hsp90 immunoprecipitation measures altered CDK4-Cdc37 complex recovery after PFKFB3 perturbation but does not display PFKFB3 in the Hsp90 precipitate, resolve the antibody's cytosolic isoform specificity, or prove pairwise binding. The strong purified binding and mutant data concern PFKFB3-CDK4, not PFKFB3-Hsp90.
claim_summary: PFKFB3 affinity-purification/mass-spectrometry discovery identified both HSP90AA1 and HSP90AB1 in main Table 2. In separate functional experiments, PFKFB3 knockdown reduced CDK4 recovery with the endogenous Hsp90-Cdc37 complex, whereas wild-type PFKFB3, but not the CDK4-binding-deficient K147A mutant, supported CDK4 association with that complex and CDK4 protein stability. These results support PFKFB3 association with and regulation of a shared cytosolic Hsp90-containing complex, but they do not establish direct PFKFB3-Hsp90 binding or an Hsp90-client relationship.

source.title: The miRISC component AGO2 has multiple binding sites for Nup358 SUMO-interacting motif.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Human HEK293T cells overexpressing HA-tagged full-length AGO2, AGO2 domains, deletion constructs, or point mutants were analyzed by HA co-immunoprecipitation and immunoblotting for endogenous HSP90; separate purified-protein and SPR experiments addressed AGO2-Nup358-SIM binding rather than HSP90.
evidence_limitations: The antibody is reported only as HSP90-specific, without gene-product resolution. Co-immunoprecipitation and mutant mapping do not establish direct binding, client status, or functional dependence, and all cellular evidence comes from one overexpression model. Purified binding assays in the paper test AGO2-SIM, not AGO2-Hsp90.
claim_summary: In HEK293T cells, HA-immunoprecipitated wild-type human AGO2 recovered endogenous HSP90. AGO2 N-domain fragments also recovered HSP90, while N-domain deletion and the L115A/V117A N-domain mutant markedly reduced recovery, mapping an HSP90-sensitive AGO2 interaction surface. This is strong current co-complex evidence for broad cytosolic Hsp90 association with AGO2, but the source does not resolve HSP90AA1 versus HSP90AB1, test purified pairwise binding, or establish Hsp90-dependent AGO2 folding, stability, or client function.

source.title: DT-Diaphorase expression and tumor cell sensitivity to 17-allylamino, 17-demethoxygeldanamycin, an inhibitor of heat shock protein 90.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Human NQO1-deficient BE colon-cancer cells and stable NQO1-restored BE-F397 derivatives were exposed to equitoxic or equimolar 17-AAG and geldanamycin concentrations; p53, RAF1, HSP70, and HSP90 were monitored by immunoblot over 6-24 hours.
evidence_limitations: The paper infers mutant p53 from high constitutive abundance without reporting TP53 sequencing, and it relies on HSP90-inhibitor pharmacology rather than direct complex, genetic perturbation, turnover-rescue, or isoform-specific assays. Prior literature, not the current experiment, supplies the established mutant-p53 client interpretation.
claim_summary: At equitoxic 17-AAG or geldanamycin concentrations, p53 protein declined in both parental and NQO1-restored BE colon-cancer cells while HSP90 abundance remained unchanged and HSP70 increased. At equal 17-AAG concentrations, p53 depletion occurred only in NQO1-high cells that were pharmacologically responsive. The authors identify the abundant baseline p53 as likely mutant and cite earlier work for mutant p53 as an HSP90 client; the current source adds inhibitor-linked depletion but no TP53-HSP90 pairwise, genetic-dependence, or isoform-resolved experiment.

source.title: Thrombin regulates vascular smooth muscle cell growth and heat shock proteins via the JAK-STAT pathway.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AB1/Hsp90beta; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Primary rat vascular smooth-muscle cells stimulated with thrombin, with STAT phosphorylation and nuclear localization, Hsp90 protein abundance, Hsp90β promoter electrophoretic mobility-shift assays, promoter-deletion reporters, AG-490 JAK2 inhibition, and dominant-negative JAK2 tested across the pathway.
evidence_limitations: The Hsp90β promoter probe resolves the regulatory target, but the protein-level anti-Hsp90 readout is generic. Anti-STAT1 abolished rather than supershifted its EMSA band, and no STAT1-specific knockdown or rescue isolates its contribution to reporter activation from STAT3, other JAK2-responsive factors, or adjacent HSF1 elements.
claim_summary: In rat vascular smooth-muscle cells, thrombin induced STAT1 phosphorylation and nuclear translocation, increased Hsp90 protein, and enhanced nuclear-protein binding to the defined STAT element in the Hsp90β promoter. In Figure 11, the faster promoter-probe complex was competed by a STAT1-inducible element and abolished by anti-STAT1 antibody. A reporter retaining the STAT-binding region was thrombin-responsive, whereas deletion of that region eliminated activation; JAK2 inhibition or dominant-negative JAK2 also blocked Hsp90β promoter activity. These current data support STAT1 as an upstream transcriptional regulator of Hsp90β in this pathway.

source.title: Thrombin regulates vascular smooth muscle cell growth and heat shock proteins via the JAK-STAT pathway.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AB1/Hsp90beta; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Primary rat vascular smooth-muscle cells stimulated with thrombin, with STAT phosphorylation and nuclear localization, Hsp90 protein abundance, Hsp90β promoter electrophoretic mobility-shift assays, promoter-deletion reporters, AG-490 JAK2 inhibition, and dominant-negative JAK2 tested across the pathway.
evidence_limitations: The Hsp90β promoter probe resolves the regulatory target, but the protein-level anti-Hsp90 readout is generic. Anti-STAT3 abolished rather than supershifted its EMSA band, and no STAT3-specific knockdown or rescue isolates its contribution to reporter activation from STAT1, other JAK2-responsive factors, or adjacent HSF1 elements.
claim_summary: In rat vascular smooth-muscle cells, thrombin induced STAT3 phosphorylation and nuclear translocation, increased Hsp90 protein, and enhanced nuclear-protein binding to the defined STAT element in the Hsp90β promoter. In Figure 11, the slower promoter-probe complex was abolished by anti-STAT3 antibody but not anti-STAT1 antibody. A reporter retaining the STAT-binding region was thrombin-responsive, whereas deletion of that region eliminated activation; JAK2 inhibition or dominant-negative JAK2 also blocked Hsp90β promoter activity. These current data support STAT3 as an upstream transcriptional regulator of Hsp90β in this pathway.

source.title: Heat shock protein 90 as an endogenous protein enhancer of inducible nitric-oxide synthase.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AB1/Hsp90beta; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Purified recombinant murine iNOS and purified bovine Hsp90 were tested biochemically; murine iNOS was coexpressed with human Hsp90beta in HEK293 cells; endogenous complexes and acute enzymatic effects were examined in LPS/interferon-gamma-induced mouse RAW264.7 macrophages, with COS-7 cytotoxicity assays as additional cellular context.
evidence_limitations: The purified Hsp90 reagent and endogenous anti-Hsp90 co-immunoprecipitation are not alpha/beta resolved, and catalytic enhancement is not a direct pairwise binding measurement. HSP90beta specificity is established only for the human overexpression experiment, while the database routes are labeled HSP90AA1. Unchanged iNOS abundance argues against inferring a canonical folding or stability client relationship from this article.
claim_summary: Purified bovine Hsp90 dose-dependently increased catalytic activity of purified recombinant murine iNOS, whereas heat-denatured Hsp90 and BSA did not. Human Hsp90beta coexpression increased iNOS-dependent nitric-oxide production in HEK293 cells without changing iNOS abundance; geldanamycin or radicicol acutely reduced iNOS activity in induced RAW264.7 macrophages, and reciprocal endogenous co-immunoprecipitation recovered iNOS with broad Hsp90. The source therefore supports an Hsp90-iNOS functional complex and allosteric enhancement rather than a protein-stability client mechanism.

source.title: Phosphorylation of serine 13 is required for the proper function of the Hsp90 co-chaperone, Cdc37.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Rabbit reticulocyte lysate was used to assemble Hsp90-Cdc37-HRI kinase complexes with recombinant wild-type or Ser13-mutant human Cdc37; endogenous phosphorylation was also examined in human K562 leukemia cells, with recombinant CK2 phosphorylation and immunoadsorption-based complex assays.
evidence_limitations: The anti-Hsp90 reagent is broad and does not resolve HSP90AA1 from HSP90AB1. Much of the mechanistic discrimination depends on Cdc37 Ser13 mutants and the HRI client in reticulocyte lysate, so the article does not establish cytosolic isoform preference or a universal effect across all Cdc37 client complexes.
claim_summary: Cdc37 was phosphorylated at Ser13 in rabbit reticulocyte lysate and K562 cells, and purified CK2 phosphorylated recombinant Cdc37 at this site. Wild-type and Ser13-mutant Cdc37 associated with broad Hsp90 in client-free lysate, but Ser13 substitution markedly impaired recruitment or retention of Cdc37 in Hsp90 complexes containing the client kinase HRI and altered complex stability and Cdc37 turnover. The data directly support CDC37 as an Hsp90 cochaperone whose Ser13 phosphorylation is required for productive kinase-client heterocomplex function.

source.title: Dissection of the mitochondrial import and assembly pathway for human Tom40.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Radiolabeled human Tom40 precursor synthesized in rabbit reticulocyte lysate was imported into isolated mitochondria from human HT1080, HeLa, and HEK293T cells. ATP depletion and purified recombinant C-terminal competitors for Hsp90-Tom70 or Hsc70 pathways were assessed by blue-native PAGE through Tom40 import and TOM-complex assembly intermediates.
evidence_limitations: The C-terminal Hsp90 dominant-negative binds Tom70 rather than TOMM40, and the study does not show Hsp90-Tom40 co-immunoprecipitation, purified pairwise binding, isoform-specific perturbation, precursor stability, or rescue. The assay addresses cytosolic chaperoning before or during mitochondrial import, not a relationship with organelle-resident TRAP1 after import.
claim_summary: ATP depletion impaired human Tom40 precursor import and assembly in isolated human mitochondria. A purified C-terminal Hsp90 fragment that dominantly blocks native cytosolic Hsp90 docking to the Tom70 receptor caused Tom40 precursor accumulation at the TOM assembly intermediate and reduced productive assembly, supporting a requirement for cytosolic Hsp90 to keep the precursor import competent. This is moderate candidate-client evidence for a pre-import TOMM40 precursor, not evidence for mitochondrial TRAP1 or a direct mature-Tom40-Hsp90 complex.

source.title: Targeting ACYP1-mediated glycolysis reverses lenvatinib resistance and restricts hepatocellular carcinoma progression.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.

Separately, ACYP1 affinity-purification mass spectrometry and co-immunoprecipitation identified a broad HSP90-containing complex, HSP90 co-immunoprecipitated with c-Myc, ACYP1 depletion weakened that association, and 17-AAG reversed ACYP1-mediated c-Myc accumulation. The current results therefore place LDHA downstream of an ACYP1-HSP90-c-Myc stability mechanism rather than demonstrating an HSP90-LDHA pair or LDHA client dependence.

These current results support FUS as a downstream HSP90/ULK1-dependent aggregate-degradation target, not an HSP90 physical partner or stability-defined client.

The paper's statement that Pgk1 physically interacts with and activates HSP90 ATPase is attributed to earlier work rather than demonstrated by a current PGK1-HSP90 pair assay.

source.title: Activation of Pgk1 Results in Reduced Protein Aggregation in Diverse Neurodegenerative Conditions.

These current experiments provide strong broad-HSP90 complex-comember evidence for ULK1 with functional autophagy support, but they do not demonstrate purified pairwise binding or ULK1 client-stability dependence.

source.title: HSP90 Exacerbates Bone Destruction in Rheumatoid Arthritis by Activating TRAF6/NFATc1 Signaling.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: RANKL-stimulated primary mouse bone-marrow macrophages with generic HSP90 cDNA overexpression or triptolide treatment, plus collagen-induced-arthritis male rat joint tissue with triptolide intervention; NFATc1 abundance and nuclear localization were measured with osteoclast differentiation readouts.
evidence_limitations: Triptolide is pleiotropic and the manuscript calls it an HSP90 middle-domain inhibitor without demonstrating exclusive target engagement. The paired HSP90 overexpression supports directionality but the cDNA, primers, and antibody are reported generically, no HSP90AA1/HSP90AB1 comparison is made, and no NFATc1-HSP90 co-immunoprecipitation, purified binding, or client-stability experiment is performed.
claim_summary: RANKL-induced mouse bone-marrow macrophages increased HSP90 and NFATc1 together. Triptolide treatment reduced HSP90, NFATc1 protein, and NFATc1 nuclear translocation, whereas HSP90 cDNA overexpression increased NFATc1 protein and nuclear localization. In collagen-induced-arthritis rat joints, HSP90, TRAF6, and NFATc1 rose together and fell with triptolide. Paired loss- and gain-of-function results therefore support NFATC1 as a strong downstream HSP90-regulated target in osteoclastogenesis, not as a demonstrated client or physical HSP90 partner.

source.title: Alantolactone curbs the malignant progression of bladder cancer partly via the HSP90AB1/LRP5/β-catenin axis.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AB1/Hsp90beta; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Human T24 and TCCSUP bladder-cancer cells, nonmalignant SV-HUC-1 urothelial cells, HSP90AB1-overexpression constructs, alantolactone and 17-AAG perturbations, MG132 proteasome inhibition, and T24/TCCSUP-derived nude-mouse tumor models were used to test the HSP90AB1-LRP5-β-catenin axis.
evidence_limitations: The co-immunoprecipitation establishes a cellular complex rather than purified pairwise binding, and no HSP90AB1 knockdown or isoform-swap rescue is shown. Alantolactone has broader cellular effects, and 17-AAG is not HSP90AB1-selective, although the overexpressed construct and immunoprecipitating antibody resolve the central pair assay to HSP90AB1.
claim_summary: In human T24 and TCCSUP bladder-cancer cells, anti-HSP90AB1 immunoprecipitation recovered LRP5, and HSP90AB1 overexpression reduced LRP5 ubiquitination, increased LRP5 abundance, activated β-catenin signaling, and rescued alantolactone-suppressed malignant phenotypes. Proteasome inhibition accumulated LRP5, while 17-AAG disrupted the HSP90AB1-LRP5 co-complex and reversed the HSP90AB1-overexpression effect on LRP5 and β-catenin pathway proteins. Together with the in-vivo HSP90AB1-overexpression rescue, these current experiments support an HSP90AB1-resolved LRP5 client-stability mechanism.

source.title: Chaperoned ubiquitylation--crystal structures of the CHIP U box E3 ubiquitin ligase and a CHIP-Ubc13-Uev1a complex.

The structural result establishes the HSP90AA1-STUB1 interface, not isoform exclusivity or client biology.
claim_summary: The current study resolves mouse CHIP/STUB1 bound to the explicit C-terminal decapeptide of human HSP90alpha and measures micromolar binding of CHIP to the HSP90 peptide and to full-length human HSP90 by isothermal titration calorimetry. The HSP90alpha peptide occupies the canonical CHIP TPR groove and establishes a direct structural cochaperone interface. Subsequent ubiquitination experiments place this interaction in a CHIP-centered HSP90 chaperoned-ubiquitylation mechanism.

In the exact HSP90 route, His-tagged HSP90 recovered Ubc13 only when CHIP was present, demonstrating a CHIP-bridged HSP90-CHIP-Ubc13 complex rather than direct HSP90-UBE2N binding. The HSP90 reagent in this ternary pull-down is not assigned to alpha or beta.

source.title: The HSP90 inhibitor 17-AAG synergizes with doxorubicin and U0126 in anaplastic large cell lymphoma irrespective of ALK expression.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Human Karpas 299, SUDHL1, and Mac2A anaplastic-large-cell-lymphoma cells exposed to 17-AAG alone or combined with doxorubicin or U0126; cell-cycle, apoptosis, signaling, and protein-abundance responses were measured by flow cytometry and immunoblotting.
evidence_limitations: The current paper uses a single HSP90 inhibitor and does not test HSP90 genetics, proteasome rescue, CDK6 half-life, physical association, purified binding, or alpha/beta-specific dependence. CDK6 depletion therefore supports a candidate downstream dependence but does not independently establish client status.
claim_summary: In three human anaplastic-large-cell-lymphoma lines, 17-AAG caused time-dependent loss of CDK6 protein together with CDK4 and cyclin D1, G0/G1 arrest, and apoptosis. This is current pharmacologic evidence that CDK6 abundance is downstream of broad cytosolic HSP90 activity in this disease model. The statement that CDK6 is chaperoned by HSP90 is supported by cited prior literature rather than a current exact-pair or turnover experiment.

source.title: A screen for deubiquitinating enzymes involved in the G₂/M checkpoint identifies USP50 as a regulator of HSP90-dependent Wee1 stability.

isoform_scope_note: Both cytosolic isoforms are compared; the scope alone does not establish an isoform-exclusive relationship.

evidence_limitations: TAP-MS establishes co-purification rather than a purified binary interaction, and the yeast-two-hybrid prey fragments are not followed by reciprocal endogenous co-immunoprecipitation. USP50 depletion affects Wee1 abundance, but the study does not directly measure HSP90-Wee1 complex occupancy, USP50 deubiquitination of a defined substrate, or isoform-specific functional dependence.
claim_summary: Tandem affinity purification of tagged full-length USP50 from U2OS cells recovered HSP90-beta as a major band identified by ten peptides, and an independent USP50-bait yeast-two-hybrid screen recovered HSP90-alpha and HSP90-beta 25 and 32 times, respectively. USP50 depletion reduced Wee1 abundance, with partial MG132 rescue, and enhanced checkpoint bypass, leading the authors to propose that USP50 regulates assembly or function of an HSP90-Wee1 complex. The two orthogonal pair assays strongly support alpha- and beta-resolved USP50 association, while the complex-regulatory mechanism remains indirect.

source.title: Phytoestrogen arctigenin preserves the mucus barrier in inflammatory bowel diseases by inhibiting goblet cell apoptosis via the ERβ/TRIM21/PHB1 pathway.

Ligand-dependent complex dissociation supports receptor-chaperone association but does not by itself establish isoform preference or a complete client mechanism.

Treatment with either arctigenin or the ERbeta agonist DPN reduced ERbeta recovery with HSP90, while the ERbeta antagonist PHTPP attenuated agonist-driven dissociation. The antibody and blot are labeled only HSP90, so the database's HSP90AA1 assignment is not source-resolved.

source.title: Cell cycle-dependent palmitoylation of protocadherin 7 by ZDHHC5 promotes successful cytokinesis.

isoform_scope_note: The evidence is Hsp90-family-wide context; no isoform specificity is inferred.

Main Figure 3A visibly labels HSP90AA1, HSP90AB1, and HSP90B1 as nodes in the PCDH7 proximity network, directly resolving all three queued source routes at the screen level. source.title: PARK7 maintains the stemness of glioblastoma stem cells by stabilizing epidermal growth factor receptor variant III

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AA1/Hsp90alpha; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Human X04 and X08 glioblastoma stem cells with PARK7 shRNA or siRNA, proteasome inhibition, EGFRvIII abundance and ubiquitination assays, endogenous PARK7-HSP90 immunoprecipitation and colocalization, plus 293T cells expressing tagged PARK7 and HSP90AA1 for co-immunoprecipitation and BiFC; downstream GSC stemness, radiation-response, and xenograft studies provide disease context.
evidence_limitations: The tagged exact-pair assays resolve HSP90AA1, whereas endogenous HSP90 experiments use a broad HSP90 label and do not compare alpha with beta. Co-immunoprecipitation and BiFC establish cellular association but not purified pairwise binding. The functional cochaperone interpretation combines PARK7-dependent EGFRvIII turnover with known EGFRvIII HSP90-client biology; the article does not show PARK7 dependence of EGFRvIII-HSP90 binding. Claim-bearing 17-AAG, HSP70-response, wild-type-EGFR, rescue, and detailed-methods material is confined to the missing supplement.
claim_summary: The current study directly tests the PARK7-HSP90 relationship. Flag-PARK7 co-immunoprecipitated Myc-HSP90AA1 in 293T cells, PARK7-HSP90AA1 BiFC produced a cellular complementation signal, and reciprocal endogenous immunoprecipitation plus immunocytochemistry confirmed PARK7 association and colocalization with broadly labeled HSP90 in two glioblastoma stem-cell lines. Separately, PARK7 knockdown reduced EGFRvIII protein without reducing its mRNA, increased EGFRvIII polyubiquitination, and enabled MG132 rescue, supporting PARK7-dependent EGFRvIII stabilization. These combined results support PARK7 as an HSP90-associated cochaperone; they do not show that PARK7 is an HSP90 client, and PARK7 knockdown did not disrupt the EGFRvIII-HSP90 complex.
