claim_summary: Using recombinant human HSP90beta and rabbit FKBP52/FKBP4, the study detected a discrete HSP90beta-FKBP52 complex by native PAGE and anti-HSP90 immunoblotting, then measured pairwise binding by surface plasmon resonance. The SPR analysis yielded an equilibrium association constant of approximately 4.1 x 10^4 M^-1, negative cooperativity, and 1:1 stoichiometry. Native PAGE did not detect a stable shifted complex under the applied conditions, and no kinetic constant or stoichiometry was derived. The result supports an HSP90beta-tested immunophilin cochaperone association, not quantitative binding strength, cellular complex function, or client status.

source.title: Quantitative assessment of complex formation of nuclear-receptor accessory proteins.

Preincubating HSP90beta with p23 altered HSP90beta binding to STIP1/Hop and shifted the modeled p60-HSP90 stoichiometry from 1:2 to 1:1 in the presence of ATP, while p23 did not bind STIP1 specifically and did not generate an additional sequential-injection sensor response. These findings support p23 as an HSP90beta-associated cochaperone that modulates complex assembly, not direct PTGES3-STIP1 binding or PTGES3 client status.

The paper's quantitative p48 experiments instead measure p48-Hsp70 binding, which did not saturate and was weakened by ATP or ADP; Figure 11 retains uncertainty around the HSP90-p48 relationship. The source therefore supports only a bounded qualitative HSP90beta-ST13 assay association within the chaperone cycle, not quantitative HSP90 binding, direct bridging, or client status.

source.title: Quantitative assessment of complex formation of nuclear-receptor accessory proteins.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AB1/Hsp90beta; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.

Quantitative p60-HSP90 and p60-Hsp70 interactions support a bridging mechanism, but weak recovery of some multicomponent complexes shows that assembly efficiency and stability depend on the artificial configuration. The database route incorrectly names HSP90AA1.
claim_summary: Recombinant STIP1/Hop/p60 bound recombinant human HSP90beta specifically and quantitatively by surface plasmon resonance, with an equilibrium association constant near 2.8 x 10^5 M^-1 without ATP, ATP-dependent changes in cooperativity, and an estimated 1:2 p60:HSP90 stoichiometry. Separate quantitative binding to Hsp70 and sequential assembly experiments support STIP1 as the bridge in a reconstituted HSP90-Hsp70 core complex. This is direct cochaperone binding and complex-assembly evidence, not evidence that STIP1 is an HSP90 client.

source.title: Post-translational disruption of the delta F508 cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR)-molecular chaperone complex with geldanamycin stabilizes delta F508 CFTR in the rabbit reticulocyte lysate.

The mutant formed a persistent hsp90-containing complex, whereas wild-type association was weaker and transient. Post-translational geldanamycin rapidly abolished hsp90 association, subsequently reduced hsc70 binding, and stabilized a fraction of deltaF508 CFTR against ubiquitination and degradation. These results support CFTR, particularly deltaF508 CFTR, as a client or chaperone substrate of a cytosolic HSP90-family complex, but the antibody and article do not resolve HSP90AA1 from HSP90AB1.

source.title: Hsp90 ensures the transition from the early Ca2+-dependent to the late phosphorylation-dependent activation of the endothelial nitric-oxide synthase in vascular endothelial growth factor-exposed endothelial cells.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.

evidence_limitations: The source uses generic Hsp90 antibodies and an unspecified Hsp90 cDNA; it does not distinguish HSP90AA1 from HSP90AB1 or reconstitute purified pairwise binding. Geldanamycin disrupted the Hsp90-eNOS-Akt complex and prevented eNOS Ser1177 phosphorylation and sustained nitric-oxide production without blocking Akt activation. Hsp90 overexpression increased eNOS-dependent nitrite production in COS-7 cells and synergized with active Akt for wild-type but not S1177A eNOS. These current experiments support a functional Hsp90-eNOS complex and regulation of eNOS activity, not a classical folding or stability client claim.

source.title: Inhibition of MDM2 by hsp90 contributes to mutant p53 stabilization.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AA1/Hsp90alpha; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Human tumor cell lines carrying multiple mutant TP53 alleles versus wild-type or null TP53, H1299 cells expressing mutant TP53 and MDM2, and p53-null versus p53/MDM2-double-null mouse fibroblasts; assays included immunoprecipitation, cycloheximide turnover, ubiquitination, proteasome inhibition, DNA damage, and MDM2 localization.
evidence_limitations: The alpha-specific antibody establishes HSP90AA1 in the mutant-p53-MDM2 complex, but HSP90AB1 was not tested and family-directed inhibitors supply the causal perturbation. The source states that MDM2 does not associate with Hsp90 without mutant p53; the proposed physical contact is indirect evidence from antibody interference rather than a purified pair assay. The effect is mutant-TP53-context dependent.

Radicicol or geldanamycin disrupted the ternary complex, increased MDM2 ubiquitination and proteasomal turnover, restored MDM2-ARF association and nucleolar localization, and enabled MDM2-dependent mutant-p53 degradation. Antibody-epitope interference suggests close Hsp90 contact with the central MDM2 region but does not establish purified direct binding. MDM2 is therefore an HSP90AA1-containing complex member and downstream regulated E3 ligase, not an Hsp90 client demonstrated by pairwise binding or folding dependence.

source.title: Inhibition of MDM2 by hsp90 contributes to mutant p53 stabilization.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AA1/Hsp90alpha; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.

The amount of Hsp90 bound to individual mutant p53 proteins correlated with their stability. Radicicol or geldanamycin disrupted the complex and promoted mutant-p53 polyubiquitination and degradation, while a p53/MDM2-double-null comparison showed that MDM2 was required for inhibitor-induced mutant-p53 turnover. This is strong mutant-specific HSP90AA1-tested client and stability evidence.

source.title: Ligand discrimination by TPR domains. Relevance and selectivity of EEVD-recognition in Hsp70 x Hop x Hsp90 complexes.

source.title: Phosphorylation and hsp90 binding mediate heat shock stabilization of p53.

The results support p53 as a broad cytosolic HSP90 client in this context but cannot assign the queued edge uniquely to HSP90AA1.

P53 immunoprecipitation recovered hsp90 after heat shock, with stronger association at two hours than four hours, while mutant p53 in DLD-1 cells provided a constitutive-complex control. Geldanamycin reduced hsp90-p53 coimmunoprecipitation and impaired heat-induced p53 accumulation, most completely in ATM-deficient cells. The current results support stress-induced p53 client or chaperone-substrate evidence at unresolved cytosolic HSP90-family scope, not an HSP90AA1-specific interaction.

source.title: ErbB2 degradation mediated by the co-chaperone protein CHIP.

source.title: Hsp90alpha recruited by Sp1 is important for transcription of 12(S)-lipoxygenase in A431 cells.

Hsp90alpha knockdown and family-wide geldanamycin perturbation reduced promoter activity and 12(S)-lipoxygenase expression. The current source supports an HSP90AA1-SP1 nuclear complex relationship, not direct binding or a client assignment.

source.title: Activity of suberoylanilide hydroxamic Acid against human breast cancer cells with amplification of her-2.

Together with dose-dependent HER2 depletion in SKBR-3 and BT-474 cells, the current experiments support ERBB2/HER2 as a cytosolic HSP90-family client whose chaperone association and turnover are perturbed by SAHA.

source.title: Activated B-RAF is an Hsp90 client protein that is targeted by the anticancer drug 17-allylamino-17-demethoxygeldanamycin.

source.title: Stat1 mediates an auto-regulation of hsp90beta gene in heat shock response.

source.title: Proteomic analyses of the SMYD family interactomes identify HSP90 as a novel target for SMYD2.

source.title: Inhibition of HSP90-dependent telomerase activity in amyloid β-induced apoptosis of cerebral endothelial cells.

model_context: Primary murine cerebral endothelial cells exposed to aggregated amyloid-beta peptides, combined HSP90-alpha/beta or TERT siRNA, geldanamycin, radicicol, MG132, serum, and AKT inhibitor; western blot, TRAP telomerase assay, TERT ubiquitination, viability, and apoptosis readouts.
evidence_limitations: The Hsp90 antibody and siRNA each combine alpha and beta and cannot resolve HSP90AA1 from HSP90AB1. The current paper does not show Hsp90-TERT co-immunoprecipitation or purified binding; physical-complex language is based on prior literature. Amyloid-beta also directly inhibits telomerase in cell extracts, so the stress phenotype is not exclusively Hsp90 mediated.
claim_summary: Amyloid-beta reduced Hsp90, TERT protein, and telomerase activity in murine cerebral endothelial cells. Combined HSP90-alpha/beta siRNA independently reduced TERT abundance and telomerase activity, while geldanamycin and radicicol potentiated telomerase inhibition and apoptosis. Amyloid-beta increased ubiquitinated TERT, and MG132 restored Hsp90 and TERT abundance together with telomerase activity. TERT siRNA also reduced telomerase activity and increased amyloid toxicity. These current orthogonal perturbations support TERT as a broad cytosolic-Hsp90 client whose stability and enzymatic activity depend on the Hsp90 system in this stress model.

source.title: HSP90 affects the stability of BMAL1 and circadian gene expression.

isoform_scope_note: Both cytosolic isoforms are mentioned without a necessarily resolved comparison; no specificity is inferred.
model_context: Mouse NIH3T3 fibroblasts carrying a Bmal1-luciferase circadian reporter, with endogenous BMAL1 and transfected BMAL1-cMyc turnover assays, four Hsp90 inhibitors, and siRNAs targeting Hsp90aa1, Hsp90ab1, Hsp90b1, Trap1, or Bmal1.
evidence_limitations: The decisive genetic experiment depletes Hsp90aa1 and Hsp90ab1 together, so it does not resolve which cytosolic isoform maintains BMAL1. Attempts to detect BMAL1-Hsp90 association in mouse liver nuclear extracts and fibroblast lysates were negative. High-dose Trap1 siRNA was toxic and excluded, and the study does not provide purified binding, single-isoform rescue, or a direct folding assay.
claim_summary: Four chemically distinct Hsp90 inhibitors altered circadian reporter rhythms, and 17-AEP-GA lowered endogenous BMAL1 abundance and shortened endogenous and cMyc-tagged BMAL1 half-lives. Simultaneous Hsp90aa1/Hsp90ab1 siRNA lowered BMAL1 nearly as strongly as Bmal1 siRNA, whereas Hsp90b1 depletion had no comparable effect and the tested low-dose Trap1 siRNA did not lower BMAL1. These results support cytosolic Hsp90-dependent BMAL1 stability and a strong candidate-client relationship, but the authors could not detect a BMAL1-Hsp90 association and explicitly retained possible indirect mechanisms.

source.title: Hepatitis C virus NS5A protein interacts with lysine methyltransferase SET and MYND domain-containing 3 and induces activator protein 1 activation.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Human Huh7/Huh7.5 hepatoma cells with overexpressed SMYD3-Myc, FLAG-HCV-NS5A, and HA-HSP90 constructs, plus HCV replicon or infection contexts and AP-1 luciferase reporter assays.
evidence_limitations: The HSP90 construct is not assigned an accession or alpha/beta gene identity, the pair evidence is one-directional co-immunoprecipitation in an overexpression system, and NS5A may bridge or stabilize a larger complex. No purified pair assay, reciprocal Hsp90 immunoprecipitation, Hsp90 perturbation, SMYD3 stability test, or Hsp90-dependent AP-1 rescue is shown.
claim_summary: Anti-Myc immunoprecipitation of SMYD3-Myc recovered HA-HSP90, and coexpressed hepatitis C virus NS5A increased normalized HSP90 recovery approximately twofold. NS5A and SMYD3 also increased AP-1 reporter activity, but Hsp90 was not perturbed in that functional assay. The current source therefore supports SMYD3 membership in an Hsp90-containing, NS5A-enhanced complex, not purified binary binding, a classical Hsp90 client mechanism, or Hsp90-causal AP-1 regulation.

source.title: PML/RARA inhibits expression of HSP90 and its target AKT.

isoform_scope_note: Both cytosolic isoforms are compared; the scope alone does not establish an isoform-exclusive relationship.
model_context: Primary acute promyelocytic leukemia marrow, PML/RARA-positive NB4 cells, PML/RARA-negative HL60 cells, zinc-inducible U937-PR9 and mock cells, and transfected HEK293T/OCI-AML2 cells; RT-qPCR, immunoblotting, promoter ChIP, ATRA/ATO treatment, and downstream AKT-turnover assays.
evidence_limitations: PML and RARA were never perturbed as separate wild-type proteins; all directionality belongs to the oncogenic PML/RARA fusion. Anti-PML ChIP identifies fusion occupancy in NB4 cells but does not establish a protein-protein interaction with HSP90 or show that PML is an HSP90 client. Broad HSP90 immunoblots do not quantify alpha and beta proteins separately, although isoform-specific transcripts and promoters are directly resolved.
claim_summary: The zinc-inducible PML/RARA fusion reduced HSP90AA1 and HSP90AB1 transcripts and broad HSP90 protein in U937-PR9 cells but not zinc-treated mock controls. In PML/RARA-positive NB4 cells, anti-PML chromatin immunoprecipitation recovered defined HSP90AA1 and HSP90AB1 promoter regions; ATRA-mediated fusion degradation reduced promoter occupancy, increased H3K14 acetylation, and restored HSP90 transcription. This supports a fusion-specific PML-component upstream transcriptional-regulator relationship for both cytosolic HSP90 isoforms, not an HSP90 client or isolated wild-type PML mechanism.

source.title: PML/RARA inhibits expression of HSP90 and its target AKT.

isoform_scope_note: Both cytosolic isoforms are compared; the scope alone does not establish an isoform-exclusive relationship.
model_context: Primary acute promyelocytic leukemia marrow, PML/RARA-positive NB4 cells, PML/RARA-negative HL60 cells, zinc-inducible U937-PR9 and mock cells, and transfected HEK293T/OCI-AML2 cells; RT-qPCR, immunoblotting, promoter ChIP, ATRA/ATO treatment, and downstream AKT-turnover assays.
evidence_limitations: PML and RARA were not perturbed separately; the regulatory activity belongs to the PML/RARA fusion. ATRA is mechanistically aligned with the RARA moiety but also degrades the fusion and activates endogenous retinoid receptors, so its effects alone cannot assign a wild-type RARA relationship. Broad HSP90 immunoblots do not separate alpha from beta protein, although both transcripts and promoter regions are resolved.
claim_summary: The zinc-inducible PML/RARA fusion reduced HSP90AA1 and HSP90AB1 transcripts and broad HSP90 protein in U937-PR9 cells but not zinc-treated mock controls. In PML/RARA-positive NB4 cells, fusion occupancy was detected at RARE-containing HSP90AA1 and HSP90AB1 promoter regions; ATRA-mediated loss of the fusion reduced occupancy, increased H3K14 acetylation, and restored HSP90 transcription. This supports a fusion-specific RARA-component upstream transcriptional-regulator relationship for both cytosolic HSP90 isoforms, not an HSP90 client or isolated wild-type RARA mechanism.

source.title: Hsp90 regulates the tumorigenic function of tyrosine protein kinase in osteosarcoma.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Human osteosarcoma patient specimens; MG63 and U2OS osteosarcoma cells with TTK or Hsp90 overexpression and shRNA; geldanamycin, 17-AAG, and MG132 perturbations; coimmunoprecipitation, immunoblotting, cell-cycle/apoptosis assays, and mouse xenografts.
evidence_limitations: The tumor-tissue correlation used an Hsp90alpha ELISA, but the cell-mechanism plasmids, shRNA, antibody, and immunoprecipitation are labeled only Hsp90 and do not establish alpha-specific dependence. Coimmunoprecipitation supports a cellular complex but not purified binary binding; inhibitor selectivity and tagged overexpression remain additional limitations.
claim_summary: Hsp90 overexpression increased TTK protein, Hsp90 knockdown reduced it, and geldanamycin or 17-AAG depleted overexpressed TTK. MG132 rescued inhibitor-induced TTK loss, while anti-Hsp90 immunoprecipitation recovered TTK and Hsp90 inhibitors weakened that association. Hsp90 inhibition also reversed TTK-driven cell-cycle, survival, proliferation, and xenograft phenotypes. Together these data support TTK as a stability-dependent cytosolic HSP90 client in osteosarcoma, with broad-HSP90 rather than defensible alpha- or beta-specific scope.

source.title: TRIM26 restricts Epstein-Barr virus infection in nasopharyngeal epithelial cells through K48-linked ubiquitination of HSP-90β.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: EBV-susceptible HNE-1, HK-1, CNE-2, and TW03 nasopharyngeal epithelial/carcinoma cells; TRIM26 overexpression or siRNA, Myc-HSP90AB1 constructs for the upstream TRIM26 mechanism, 17-AAG and geldanamycin treatment, immunoblotting, surface-EphA2 flow cytometry, and EBV infection assays.
evidence_limitations: HSP90AB1 specificity is established for the upstream TRIM26 ubiquitination substrate, while the direct EPHA2 perturbation uses pan-HSP90 inhibitors. Parallel movement of HSP90beta and EphA2 after TRIM26 manipulation plus inhibitor-dependent EphA2 loss supports pathway direction but does not demonstrate binary contact, direct chaperoning, or exclude an HSP90AA1 contribution.
claim_summary: TRIM26 overexpression decreased HSP90beta and EphA2 protein, whereas TRIM26 knockdown increased both. EBV raised HSP90beta abundance, and the broad HSP90 inhibitors 17-AAG and geldanamycin reduced endogenous EphA2 in time- and dose-dependent experiments and reduced EBV entry. The paper therefore supports EPHA2 as a downstream protein-maintenance target of an HSP90AB1-centered TRIM26 pathway, but it does not show an HSP90beta-EPHA2 coimmunoprecipitation, purified interaction, or direct HSP90AB1 genetic perturbation and should not establish a physical client pair by itself.

source.title: HSP90β shapes the fate of Th17 cells with the help of glycolysis-controlled methylation modification.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AB1/Hsp90beta; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Mouse naive CD4-positive T cells differentiated under Th17 or Treg conditions, DSS colitis mice, and human ulcerative-colitis expression datasets; VER-82576, shHSP90beta, HSP90beta overexpression, GLUT1/lactate/TET2/STAT5 rescue or epistasis, RT-qPCR, immunoblotting, flow cytometry, ChIP-PCR, bisulfite sequencing, and methylation/5-hydroxymethylcytosine assays.
evidence_limitations: The exact HSP90beta physical client demonstrated in the mechanism is GLUT1, not FOXP3. FOXP3 responds through a multistep metabolic and chromatin pathway, and the selective-inhibitor result is strengthened but not made physically direct by shRNA and overexpression. Most mechanistic work is in mouse T cells and a DSS-colitis model rather than human primary T cells.
claim_summary: The HSP90beta-selective inhibitor VER-82576 and shHSP90beta increased Foxp3 RNA, protein, and Foxp3-positive T-cell frequency under Th17 conditions, whereas HSP90beta overexpression reversed this shift. Main Figures 5-7 link that directional response to reduced GLUT1-dependent glycolysis and lactate, increased STAT5/TET2 occupancy at Foxp3 CNS2, lower CNS2 methylation, and increased Foxp3 transcription, with rescue and epistasis experiments. This is strong HSP90AB1-resolved downstream transcriptional and epigenetic regulation of FOXP3, not an HSP90beta-FOXP3 physical interaction or folding-client relationship.

source.title: A cyclophilin function in Hsp90-dependent signal transduction.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Saccharomyces cerevisiae expressing heterologous viral pp60v-Src or cellular pp60c-Src, with CPR6/CPR7, HSC82, HSP82, and STI1 deletion or mutant backgrounds; GST pulldown, growth genetics, Src abundance, and phosphotyrosine readouts.
evidence_limitations: The current v-Src panel perturbs the Hsp90 cochaperone Cpr7 rather than Hsp90 itself and does not demonstrate an Hsp90-v-Src co-immunoprecipitate or purified pair. Direct Hsp90 dependence of v-Src is cited from earlier yeast studies. The model uses viral Src in yeast Hsc82/Hsp82 machinery and cannot resolve human HSP90AA1 versus HSP90AB1.
claim_summary: In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Cpr6 and Cpr7 bound yeast Hsp90 through their TPR-containing C termini, including in bacterial lysates lacking other yeast proteins. Deletion of CPR7 genetically aggravated reduced-Hsp90 and STI1 backgrounds. When viral pp60v-Src was expressed in cpr7-null cells, both its abundance and kinase-dependent cellular tyrosine phosphorylation were reduced; cpr6 deletion reduced activity without reducing abundance, while cellular c-Src was unaffected. These current results support v-Src as an Hsp90-machinery-dependent client whose stability and activity require the Cpr7 cyclophilin cochaperone in yeast.

source.title: Combination of pan-histone deacetylase inhibitor and autophagy inhibitor exerts superior efficacy against triple-negative human breast cancer cells.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Human MB-231 and SUM159PT triple-negative breast-cancer cells plus MB-231 xenograft tumors, with broad Hsp90 immunoprecipitation, panobinostat perturbation, immunoblotting, autophagy assays, and survival phenotyping.
evidence_limitations: The immunoprecipitating antibody is labeled Hsp90 without alpha/beta discrimination, no reciprocal HDAC6 capture or purified binding is shown, and HDAC6 is not genetically perturbed. The exact HSP90AA1 database route is therefore source-scope unresolved.
claim_summary: Broad Hsp90 immunoprecipitation from MB-231 tumors and cells recovers HDAC6 together with HSF1 and p97, and panobinostat dose-dependently disrupts the Hsp90-HDAC6-containing complex in two triple-negative breast-cancer lines. This supports HDAC6 as a member of a broad cytosolic Hsp90 complex, not direct pairwise binding, client status, or an HSP90AA1-specific route.

source.title: Characterization of the interaction of Aha1 with components of the Hsp90 chaperone machine and client proteins.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Rabbit reticulocyte lysate with translated His-tagged Aha1 and native Hsp90 complexes, plus HeLa-cell Flag-Aha1 complexes and Hsp90-dependent luciferase-renaturation assays.
evidence_limitations: All Hsp90 reagents and author claims are broad, so the HSP90AA1 database mapping cannot be preserved as isoform-specific. Salt-sensitive co-complex recovery supports cochaperone association but is not itself purified pairwise binding, and AHSA1 should not be treated as a client.
claim_summary: His-tagged Aha1 co-adsorbs endogenous Hsp90 from rabbit reticulocyte lysate, molybdate stabilizes the association, high salt and Hsp90 inhibitors disrupt it, and Hsp90-directed immunoprecipitation reciprocally recovers Aha1. Additional experiments place Aha1 with selected Hsp90 cochaperones and show functional effects on Hsp90-dependent luciferase renaturation. The source strongly supports AHSA1 as a broad Hsp90 cochaperone but does not resolve HSP90AA1 from HSP90AB1.

source.title: A regulatory circuit that involves HR23B and HDAC6 governs the biological response to HDAC inhibitors.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Human U937 leukemia cells treated with HDAC inhibitors or 17-AAG, plus HEK293T tagged-HDAC6 interaction assays; AP-MS, co-immunoprecipitation, immunoblotting, apoptosis, and HR23B abundance readouts.
evidence_limitations: The current source establishes complex membership, not purified direct binding or client status. It does not distinguish HSP90AA1 from HSP90AB1 and supplies no GRP94/HSP90B1-specific reagent or ER-compartment result. Functional interpretation partly depends on pan-Hsp90 pharmacology.
claim_summary: Unbiased HDAC6 affinity proteomics identified HSP90, and current Figure 5e confirms that HSP90 co-immunoprecipitates with tagged HDAC6. Hsp90 inhibition with 17-AAG prevents HDAC6-dependent HR23B loss and restores apoptosis. The antibody and text use broad HSP90 wording, so the current source supports an HDAC6-Hsp90 complex but not the queued alpha, beta, or ER-GRP94 routes individually.

source.title: Glucocorticoid receptor function regulated by coordinated action of the Hsp90 and Hsp70 chaperone cycles.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AA1/Hsp90alpha; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Purified human Hsp90alpha, full-length human HSPA1A/Hsp70, Hop, Hsp40, p23, and glucocorticoid-receptor ligand-binding domain in biochemical reconstitution, pull-down, SEC-MALS, ligand-binding, and approximately 38-angstrom cryo-EM experiments.
evidence_limitations: The structural density is low resolution and demonstrates contact within a multicomponent cycle rather than a purified binary Hsp90-Hsp70 interaction. HSP90AA1 is the assayed isoform, but alpha exclusivity over HSP90AB1 is not tested.
claim_summary: The reconstituted human glucocorticoid-receptor chaperone cycle uses HSPA1A-encoded Hsp70 and HSP90AA1-encoded Hsp90alpha. HSPA1A binds and partially unfolds GRLBD, whereas Hsp90alpha, Hsp70, Hop, and GRLBD form a defined complex that reverses Hsp70 inhibition. Pull-down, SEC-MALS, and low-resolution cryo-EM place the Hsp70 nucleotide-binding domain between the Hsp90 N-terminal domains, directly supporting HSPA1A as an HSP90AA1 chaperone-cycle component.

source.title: Methyl-deficient diet promotes colitis and SIRT1-mediated endoplasmic reticulum stress.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Methyl-donor-deficient and DSS-treated rat colitis models, human Caco-2 intestinal epithelial cells with SIRT1 siRNA, SRT1720 activation in vitro and in vivo, and human inflammatory-bowel-disease tissue context.
evidence_limitations: The HSP90 antibody and expression readout do not resolve HSP90AA1 from HSP90AB1, and the effect is regulatory rather than pairwise. SRT1720 is pharmacologic, but the two-siRNA experiment supplies independent directionality. ER-stress context does not make this GRP94 evidence.
claim_summary: Two independent SIRT1 siRNAs reduce broad HSP90 protein in Caco-2 cells while activating unfolded-protein-response markers. Methyl-donor deficiency lowers SIRT1 and hyperacetylates HSF1 in rats, whereas the SIRT1 activator SRT1720 restores HSP90 and other chaperones in vitro and in vivo. The data support SIRT1 as an upstream regulator of Hsp90 expression through HSF1 state, not as an Hsp90 client or direct partner.

source.title: Widespread macromolecular interaction perturbations in human genetic disorders.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AB1/Hsp90beta; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Human HEK293T/HEK293T-derived interaction assays expressing wild-type or disease-associated AMPD3 variants, with HSP90beta LUMIER, co-immunoprecipitation, immunoblot, and cellular thermal-stability measurements.
evidence_limitations: The evidence is specific to W450R and A320V variants and does not establish a general wild-type AMPD3-HSP90AB1 edge. Hsp90 is not genetically or pharmacologically perturbed, and increased association plus reduced thermal stability does not by itself prove folding rescue or turnover control.
claim_summary: The LUMIER chaperone assay explicitly uses HSP90beta/HSP90AB1. AMPD3 variants W450R and A320V show increased association with endogenous HSP90beta relative to wild-type AMPD3, with differential interaction scores of 9.4 and 2.1, respectively. Both variants are less thermally stable than wild type, supporting variant-specific recruitment to HSP90AB1 as a candidate-client response to destabilization.

source.title: CHK2-BRCA1 tumor-suppressor axis restrains oncogenic Aurora-A kinase to ensure proper mitotic microtubule assembly.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Human U2OS osteosarcoma cells and mitotic extracts used for BRCA1 SILAC immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry, followed by focused CHK2, AURKA, BARD1, PP6, and microtubule-assembly assays.
evidence_limitations: HSP90 is a named current AP-MS positive-control hit rather than a mechanistic focus and lacks an Hsp90-specific reciprocal assay, perturbation, or isoform-resolving reagent. The source cannot support the queued ER-GRP94 route or separate alpha from beta.
claim_summary: Current SILAC BRCA1 immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry recovered HSP90 among 515 BRCA1-associated proteins and cites it as a known BRCA1-interactor positive control. This supports broad Hsp90 complex membership with BRCA1 in the current source, but the article does not identify the HSP90 isoform or test any exact HSP90AA1, HSP90AB1, or HSP90B1 route independently.

source.title: HSP90 is necessary for the ACK1-dependent phosphorylation of STAT1 and STAT3.

isoform_scope_note: Both cytosolic isoforms are mentioned without a necessarily resolved comparison; no specificity is inferred.
model_context: Human LNCaP and other prostate-cancer cells plus HEK293T tagged-ACK1 assays, with SILAC AP-MS, reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation, AT13387 treatment, ACK1 abundance/phosphorylation, and downstream STAT readouts.
evidence_limitations: The physical assays resolve alpha and beta recovery but do not prove binary direct binding. Functional dependence uses a pan-Hsp90 inhibitor without genetic rescue, turnover kinetics, or individual isoform perturbation, so client status remains candidate-level and cannot be assigned separately to alpha versus beta.
claim_summary: SILAC MYC-ACK1 immunoprecipitation enriches both HSP90AA1 and HSP90AB1, and reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation validates an ACK1-Hsp90 alpha/beta complex. The Hsp90 inhibitor AT13387 reduces total and phosphorylated ACK1 with downstream loss of phospho-STAT1 and phospho-STAT3, supporting TNK2/ACK1 as a candidate client whose abundance and signaling activity depend on cytosolic Hsp90.

source.title: Ubiquilin 2 modulates ALS/FTD-linked FUS-RNA complex dynamics and stress granule formation.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AA1/Hsp90alpha; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Doxycycline-inducible FLAG-UBQLN2 HEK293T cells analyzed by SILAC anti-FLAG purification and nLC-MS/MS, followed by STRING organization of stress-granule-associated UBQLN2-enriched proteins and focused FUS validation.
evidence_limitations: HSP90AA1 is a displayed screen hit, not one of the interactors independently validated. STRING edges in Figure 1E represent prior network connectivity among recovered proteins rather than direct UBQLN2-HSP90AA1 binding. HSP90AB1 and TRAP1 are not reported in the main source.
claim_summary: FLAG-UBQLN2 SILAC immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry identified 181 putative interactors enriched more than 1.5-fold over control. HSP90AA1 is explicitly displayed in Figure 1E within the molecular-chaperone subset of UBQLN2-enriched stress-granule-associated proteins. The source therefore supports an HSP90AA1-resolved screen association with tagged UBQLN2, but it does not display HSP90AB1 or TRAP1 and does not validate HSP90AA1 by pairwise immunoblot or functional testing.

source.title: Exosomes Derived from Endoplasmic Reticulum Stressed Hepatocellular Carcinoma Cells Enhance the Antitumor Immunity of Dendritic Cells.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Human HepG2 hepatocellular-carcinoma cells with tunicamycin-induced ER stress, purified tumor-cell exosomes, stable donor-cell HSP90 shRNA, human dendritic cells, flow-cytometric maturation markers, and lymphocyte tumor-lysis assays.
evidence_limitations: The shRNA and validation antibody are labeled generically as HSP90, so the genetic effect cannot be assigned to HSP90AA1 or HSP90AB1 despite both isoforms appearing in the proteomic profile. CD80 is measured only in recipient dendritic cells and is not tested for binding or chaperoning.
claim_summary: LC-MS/MS identifies HSP90AA1 and HSP90AB1 as enriched in exosomes from ER-stressed HepG2 cells, and a generic HSP90 immunoblot validates exosomal abundance. Stable HSP90 shRNA in donor tumor cells reduces exosomal HSP90 and weakens recipient dendritic-cell CD80 induction and antitumor function. CD80 is therefore a downstream maturation readout of exosomal cytosolic Hsp90 signaling, not a direct partner or client.

source.title: A novel cytoplasmic protein that interacts with the Ah receptor, contains tetratricopeptide repeat motifs, and augments the transcriptional response to 2,3,7,8-tetrachlorodibenzo-p-dioxin.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Mouse hepatoma wild-type, Arnt-defective, and AhR-defective cell lines expressed T7-tagged AIP; AIP complexes, TCDD-dependent complex dynamics, and CYP1A1 transcriptional responses were examined. Purified and yeast-two-hybrid experiments directly resolved AIP-AhR rather than AHR-Hsp90.
evidence_limitations: The decisive Hsp90 result is recovery in an AIP-bait co-immunoprecipitate, so the source establishes cellular co-complex membership rather than direct pairwise AHR-Hsp90 binding. The Hsp90 antibody and wording are broad and cannot validate the database's HSP90AA1-specific annotation. No HSP90 perturbation, AHR turnover, or alpha/beta comparison establishes a canonical client relationship.
claim_summary: AIP-T7 immunoprecipitation from mouse hepatoma cells recovered both AhR and Hsp90 in the unliganded state. TCDD disrupted the AIP-AhR-Hsp90 complex in wild-type cells, whereas altered behavior in Arnt-defective and AhR-defective cells helped distinguish ligand and receptor requirements. Together with AIP-AhR yeast-two-hybrid and purified-binding results and enhanced CYP1A1 transcription after AIP expression, the source supports AHR and broad cytosolic Hsp90 as members of a ligand-regulated AIP-containing complex, but it does not show purified AHR-Hsp90 binding or resolve HSP90AA1 from HSP90AB1.

source.title: GALNT5 uaRNA promotes gastric cancer progression through its interaction with HSP90.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Human gastric-cancer cell lines, RNA pulldown and RIP, recombinant binding, coimmunoprecipitation, ubiquitination/abundance assays, xenografts, and HSP90-knockdown epistasis.
evidence_limitations: The antibody and recombinant construct are labelled only as HSP90, so HSP90AA1 versus HSP90AB1 is unresolved. The bound entity is GALNT5 uaRNA rather than the GALNT5 protein; the result must not be recast as a GALNT5 protein client relationship.
claim_summary: GALNT5 uaRNA, a noncoding transcript from the GALNT5 3-prime UTR, binds broad HSP90 in RNA-pulldown/MS, HSP90 immunoblot and RIP assays, and a recombinant GST-HSP90 binding assay. GALNT5 uaRNA abundance alters HSP90 association with AKT and IKK and their ubiquitination, while HSP90 knockdown suppresses the proliferation, migration, and invasion phenotype caused by GALNT5 uaRNA overexpression.

source.title: The HSP90 inhibitor 17-DMAG alleviates primary biliary cholangitis via cholangiocyte necroptosis prevention.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: Human intrahepatic bile-duct epithelial cells exposed to GCDCA and LPS, with HSP90 siRNA, 17-DMAG, viability/flow-cytometry assays, and necroptosis-marker immunoblots; patient and mouse PBC tissue provides disease context.
evidence_limitations: No HSP90 isoform is resolved, the in vivo work is inhibitor-only, and direct HSP90-RIPK3 binding or RIPK3 half-life rescue is not shown. The direct chaperone/turnover evidence in this paper is for RIPK1.
claim_summary: In human cholangiocytes, HSP90 siRNA and 17-DMAG reduce toxic-bile-acid/LPS-induced necroptosis and lower phosphorylated RIPK3 together with RIPK1 and phosphorylated MLKL. The current source directly identifies RIPK1, not RIPK3, in an HSP90 IP/HPLC-MS complex; RIPK3 is therefore a downstream pathway target rather than a demonstrated HSP90-binding client.

source.title: Adamantyl-substituted retinoid-related molecules bind small heterodimer partner and modulate the Sin3A repressor.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
model_context: MDA-MB-468 nuclear extracts and intact-cell SHP-SIN3A repressor-complex assays after 3-Cl-AHPC treatment, with co-IP, immunoblot, inhibitor, and SIN3A-knockdown readouts.
evidence_limitations: The HSP90 reagent remains generic, the complex is multicomponent, and the recovered supplementary figures do not test purified HSP90-SIN3A binding or isoform-selective dependence.
claim_summary: The main article shows drug-enhanced recovery of generic HSP90 with immunoprecipitated SIN3A complexes. Recovered Supplementary Figures 2 and 3 confirm additional TBL1/GPS2 recruitment and effective SIN3A knockdown, closing the source-package hold without resolving HSP90AA1 versus HSP90AB1.

source.title: Characterization of the human COP9 signalosome complex using affinity purification and mass spectrometry.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AB1/Hsp90beta; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: HBTH-CSN5 affinity purification in human 293 cells with tag-only controls and complementary MAP-SILAC/PAM-SILAC quantitative proteomics.
evidence_limitations: The study supports association with a CSN5-containing COP9 signalosome complex, not purified pairwise binding, HSP90 client status, or a functional requirement for HSP90AB1.
claim_summary: Supplemental Tables 1-2 identify P08238/HSP90AB1 in CSN5-containing affinity purifications and place it in the authors' stable-interactor class. Displayed quantitative runs show 17, 11, and 21 unique peptides with average SILAC ratios of 2.0, 1.8, and 2.1, respectively.

source.title: Direct binding of CoREST1 to SUMO-2/3 contributes to gene-specific repression by the LSD1/CoREST1/HDAC complex.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AB1/Hsp90beta; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.

evidence_limitations: The HSP90AB1 entry is a two-peptide discovery-screen hit without HSP90-focused validation. It does not reproduce BioGRID's reconstituted-complex wording, establish purified pairwise binding, or show client dependence.
claim_summary: Supplemental Table 1 lists HSP90AB1 (NP_031381.2) with two peptides among proteins recovered by SUMO-2 affinity chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry.

source.title: Proteomic analysis of the NOS2 interactome in human airway epithelial cells.

isoform_scope_note: Both cytosolic isoforms are compared; the scope alone does not establish an isoform-exclusive relationship.
model_context: Anti-FLAG affinity capture of catalytically inactive E377Q-NOS2 in cytokine-stimulated A549 cells followed by GeLC-MS/MS and SILAC quantification.
evidence_limitations: The source does not establish purified HSP90-NOS2 binding, client stability, HSP90 perturbation, or isoform preference, and uses overexpressed inactive NOS2 in one cancer-derived cell line.
claim_summary: Recovered Tables S1-S2 resolve both cytosolic isoforms in the NOS2 affinity capture. Table S2 reports HSP90AA1 with 37 SILAC pairs, 61 unique peptides, 1.468-fold cytokine-associated change, and p=0; HSP90AB1 has 25 pairs, 46 unique peptides, 1.501-fold change, and p=3.098e-28.

source.title: Tetraspanin CD9 stabilizes gp130 by preventing its ubiquitin-dependent lysosomal degradation to promote STAT3 activation in glioma stem cells.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AA1/Hsp90alpha; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.

source.title: HSF-1 Interacts with Ral-binding Protein 1 in a Stress-responsive, Multiprotein Complex with HSP90 in Vivo.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.

evidence_limitations: The source does not resolve HSP90AA1 versus HSP90AB1 as the biological isoform and does not establish direct RALBP1-HSP90 binding or client dependence.

This supports RALBP1 as a cytosolic HSP90-containing complex member/stress-response context, not direct HSP90-RALBP1 binding and not client evidence.

source.title: The piR-31115-PIWIL4 complex promotes the migration of the triple-negative breast cancer cell line MDA-MB-231 by suppressing HSP90AA1 degradation.

This is HSP90AA1-resolved upstream-stabilization/direct-partner evidence for PIWIL4, not evidence that PIWIL4 is an HSP90 client.

source.title: Interaction between Casein Kinase II and the 90-kDa Stress Protein, HSP90.

This supports CKII alpha/CSNK2A1-like cytosolic HSP90 direct-partner/chaperone-function evidence, not alpha/beta isoform-resolved HSP90 evidence.

source.title: Regulation of mitochondrial complex III activity and assembly by TRAP1 in cancer cells.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves TRAP1; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: HeLa/HCT116 cancer cell mitochondrial TRAP1 perturbation and complex III activity/assembly assays under basal and low-glucose conditions.
evidence_limitations: This supports TRAP1-UQCRC2 binding and complex III regulation, not UQCRC2 stability as a TRAP1 client.
claim_summary: TRAP1 binds UQCRC2 by GFP-trap, endogenous mitochondrial IP, PLA, and FLIM/FRET, and modulates complex III activity/assembly under metabolic stress without changing UQCRC2 abundance.

source.title: Essential role of the molecular chaperone gp96 in regulating melanogenesis.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90B1/GRP94; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Melanocyte/melanoma and Hsp90b1 loss models with pigmentation, melanosome maturation, and Wnt-rescue assays.
evidence_limitations: LRP6-specific maturation evidence is largely carried from prior GRP94-LRP6 sources rather than newly demonstrated in this source.
claim_summary: The current source tests gp96/GRP94 loss in melanogenesis and Wnt-associated phenotypes and invokes prior gp96-LRP6 maturation biology; it supports tissue-context reinforcement for the LRP6 route but not a fresh LRP6 client anchor.

source.title: Degradation of AIMP1/p43 induced by hepatitis C virus E2 leads to upregulation of TGF-beta signaling and increase in surface expression of gp96.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90B1/GRP94; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: HCV E2 viral-protein perturbation, AIMP1 degradation, AIMP1 knockdown, and gp96 surface-localization assays.
evidence_limitations: The cleaner direct AIMP1-gp96 retention anchor remains the earlier primary AIMP1/gp96 source; this paper is viral-perturbation directional support.
claim_summary: HCV E2 interacts with and promotes degradation of AIMP1/p43, and AIMP1 loss or E2 expression increases surface gp96/GRP94; the current source supports AIMP1 as a gp96 localization/surface-presentation regulator, not as a client.

source.title: Quantitative glycoproteomics reveals new classes of STT3A- and STT3B-dependent N-glycosylation sites.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90B1/GRP94; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: STT3A/STT3B-deficient cellular glycoproteomics and N-glycosylation-site classification.
evidence_limitations: Evidence concerns HSP90B1/GRP94 glycosylation-site context, not an HSP90B1-STT3A protein interaction.
claim_summary: Quantitative glycoproteomics places HSP90B1/GRP94 glycosylation in the STT3A/STT3B-dependent N-glycosylation landscape; STT3A is glycosylation-machinery support, not a GRP94 client or binding partner.

source.title: Quantitative glycoproteomics reveals new classes of STT3A- and STT3B-dependent N-glycosylation sites.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90B1/GRP94; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: STT3A/STT3B-deficient cellular glycoproteomics and N-glycosylation-site classification.
evidence_limitations: Evidence concerns HSP90B1/GRP94 glycosylation-site context, not an HSP90B1-STT3B protein interaction.
claim_summary: Quantitative glycoproteomics places HSP90B1/GRP94 glycosylation in the STT3A/STT3B-dependent N-glycosylation landscape; STT3B is glycosylation-machinery support, not a GRP94 client or binding partner.

source.title: GM2-GM3 gangliosides ratio is dependent on GRP94 through down-regulation of GM2-AP cofactor in brain metastasis cells.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90B1/GRP94; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: GRP94 silencing in brain-metastasis cells with GM2-AP protein and ganglioside-ratio readouts.
evidence_limitations: Client-like status is author-interpreted and lacks direct GRP94-GM2A binding, maturation, folding, or rescue evidence.
claim_summary: GRP94 silencing lowers GM2-AP/GM2A protein in a ganglioside-metabolism context and the authors propose that GM2-AP could be a GRP94 client, but direct binding or maturation assays are not shown.

source.title: Honokiol bis-dichloroacetate is a selective allosteric inhibitor of the mitochondrial chaperone TRAP1.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves TRAP1; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: TRAP1-selective HDCA inhibitor studies in tumor-cell mitochondrial metabolism models.
evidence_limitations: SIRT3 support is pharmacologic/metabolic context downstream of a TRAP1 inhibitor, not direct interaction or client evidence.
claim_summary: HDCA selectively inhibits TRAP1 and reverses TRAP1-dependent SDH suppression; SIRT3 is induced in the same pharmacologic mitochondrial-response axis, but no TRAP1-SIRT3 binding or client relationship is shown.

source.title: Tumor growth of neurofibromin-deficient cells is driven by decreased respiration and hampered by NAD+ and SIRT3.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves TRAP1; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: NF1-deficient MEFs and MPNST models with TRAP1 knockout, SIRT3 overexpression, NAD manipulation, respiration, SDH, and tumorigenicity assays.
evidence_limitations: The source supports functional metabolic cross-talk, not a TRAP1-SIRT3 physical interaction, cochaperone relationship, or client-dependence mechanism.
claim_summary: In NF1-deficient tumor models, SIRT3 overexpression or NAD replenishment and TRAP1 knockout converge on mitochondrial respiration/SDH activity and antineoplastic phenotypes, supporting functional pathway-level TRAP1-SIRT3 cross-talk but not direct binding or client biology.

source.title: The chaperone activity of GRP94 toward insulin-like growth factor II is necessary for the stress response to serum deprivation.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90B1/GRP94; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: GRP94-deficient and rescued embryonic stem cell models under serum deprivation, plus pro-IGF-II expression/processing assays.
evidence_limitations: Evidence is ER/secretory-pathway and stress-context specific; it should not be collapsed into cytosolic HSP90 evidence.
claim_summary: The source shows that GRP94/HSP90B1 physically and transiently interacts with pro-IGF-II intermediates and is required for processing/secretion of active IGF-II during serum-deprivation stress. This is corrected from a noisy GRP alias route to IGF2.

source.title: Protein C mutation (A267T) results in ER retention and unfolded protein response activation.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90B1/GRP94; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: CHO-K1 stable-expression models comparing wild-type protein C with the A267T disease mutant.
evidence_limitations: Association is increased for the mutant, but no GRP94 perturbation/rescue test establishes PROC as a validated GRP94 client.
claim_summary: The PROC A267T mutant is retained in the ER and shows increased association with GRP94 and calreticulin after crosslinking, with impaired secretion and UPR activation. The source does not prove GRP94-dependent folding or rescue.

source.title: Glucose-regulated protein 94 triage of mutant myocilin through endoplasmic reticulum-associated degradation subverts a more efficient autophagic clearance mechanism.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90B1/GRP94; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: HEK inducible and transient-expression models comparing wild-type MYOC with glaucoma-associated mutant myocilin variants.
evidence_limitations: Evidence is mutant/disease-allele specific and should not be generalized to wild-type MYOC client status without additional support.
claim_summary: Disease-associated mutant myocilin is specifically recognized by GRP94 and triaged through ERAD; GRP94 depletion or inhibition reduces mutant myocilin by shifting clearance toward autophagy. Wild-type myocilin is not the supported target state.

source.title: Limitation of individual folding resources in the ER leads to outcomes distinct from the unfolded protein response.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90B1/GRP94; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Cell-culture GRP94 depletion/inhibition compared with BiP, HSP47, PDIA6, and OS-9 silencing and ER-stress treatments.
evidence_limitations: The source supports a downstream response to GRP94 limitation, not HSPA5 client dependence or direct HSPA5-GRP94 binding.
claim_summary: GRP94/HSP90B1 depletion or inhibition selectively induces BiP/HSPA5 and PDIA6 without a broad canonical UPR. This supports HSPA5 as a GRP94-perturbation response marker, not a GRP94 client or direct interactor.

source.title: Perturbations in maturation of secretory proteins and their association with endoplasmic reticulum chaperones in a cell culture model for epithelial ischemia.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90B1/GRP94; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Kidney ischemia and antimycin A-treated thyroid epithelial cell culture models of epithelial ischemia/ATP depletion.
evidence_limitations: Evidence is stress/ATP-depletion specific and shared across ER chaperones; it should not be treated as ordinary wild-type GRP94 client evidence.
claim_summary: ATP depletion/antimycin A in epithelial ischemia models inhibits thyroglobulin secretion and causes TG to associate in ER-localized macromolecular complexes with BiP, GRP94, and ERp72. This is stress-associated GRP94/TG support, not a normal-state client proof.

source.title: Proteostasis regulators restore function of epilepsy-associated GABAA receptors.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90B1/GRP94; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: HEK293T, SH-SY5Y, rat primary neuron, and heterosynapse assays with epilepsy-associated GABA-A receptor mutants.
evidence_limitations: Drug/remodeling evidence supports mutant alpha1 proteostasis in a GRP94-associated ERAD pathway, but not a final generalized GABRA1 client call.
claim_summary: Proteostasis regulators reduce degradation and improve trafficking/function of mutant GABA-A receptor alpha1 subunits; the source places alpha1(A322D) in a GRP94/Hrd1/Sel1L/VCP ERAD pathway and shows altered interactions with GRP94/VCP after treatment.

source.title: Oocyte-targeted deletion reveals that hsp90b1 is needed for the completion of first mitosis in mouse zygotes.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90B1/GRP94; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Mouse oocyte-specific Hsp90b1 deletion and early zygote development assays.
evidence_limitations: The paper does not show HSPA5 as an HSP90B1 client or direct partner; HSPA5 is a non-compensating ER-chaperone response marker.
claim_summary: HSPA5/BiP is increased in Hsp90b1 mutant oocytes/embryos but does not compensate for the HSP90B1-dependent first-mitosis and ER/cytoskeleton defects. This is compensatory response support, not HSPA5-GRP94 client evidence.

source.title: Multi-chaperone function modulation and association with cytoskeletal proteins are key features of the function of AIP in the pituitary gland.

isoform_scope_note: Both cytosolic isoforms are compared; the scope alone does not establish an isoform-exclusive relationship.
model_context: Rat GH3 pituitary-cell lysate AIP pull-down/MS, AIP co-IP/localization validation, and AIP variant interaction assays.
evidence_limitations: The source supports AIP as a cochaperone/direct partner; it should not be reinterpreted as an HSP90 client.
claim_summary: AIP pull-down/MS and validation experiments support AIP association with HSP90AA1 and HSP90AB1, plus HSPA8, and disease-linked AIP variants impair selected chaperone-network interactions. This is AIP cochaperone/direct-partner evidence, not client evidence.

source.title: Myeloid endoplasmic reticulum resident chaperone GP96 facilitates inflammation and steatosis in alcohol-associated liver disease.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90B1/GRP94; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Human alcohol-associated hepatitis liver samples, alcohol-fed mouse liver, myeloid GP96 knockout, and macrophage GP96 inhibitor/siRNA assays.
evidence_limitations: No HSPA5-GP96 direct binding, folding, maturation, or client-dependence assay is shown.
claim_summary: GP96/HSP90B1 is functionally tested in alcohol-associated liver disease models, and HSPA5/GRP78 is co-induced or compensatorily increased after GP96 loss. This supports HSPA5 as ER-stress/compensatory response context, not as a GP96 client.

source.title: Protein interactome analysis of ATP1B1 in alveolar epithelial cells using Co-Immunoprecipitation mass spectrometry and parallel reaction monitoring assay.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AB1/Hsp90beta; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: A549 alveolar epithelial ATP1B1 Co-IP/MS, PRM candidate validation, and endogenous ATP1B1-HSP90AB1 co-IP.
evidence_limitations: The source does not show ATP1B1 folding, maturation, stability, localization dependence, or HSP90 inhibitor sensitivity.
claim_summary: ATP1B1 co-IP/MS identifies HSP90AB1 among ATP1B1-associated proteins, PRM supports selected candidates, and endogenous co-IP confirms ATP1B1-HSP90AB1 association in A549 cells. This is HSP90AB1 direct/complex-partner evidence for ATP1B1, not client evidence.

source.title: Sex-specific effects of alcohol on neurobehavioral performance and endoplasmic reticulum stress: an analysis using neuron-specific MANF deficient mice.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90B1/GRP94; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Adult neuron-specific MANF knockout mice with acute binge alcohol exposure and sex/time-stratified ER-stress marker assays.
evidence_limitations: The source does not show MANF-GRP94 binding or MANF as a GRP94 client; it is regulatory/stress-response evidence only.
claim_summary: Neuron-specific MANF deficiency and alcohol exposure alter ER homeostasis and increase GRP94/HSP90B1 expression in sex- and time-dependent contexts. This supports MANF as an upstream ER-stress regulator/readout context for GRP94, not as a GRP94 client or direct partner.

source.title: The co-chaperone Cdc37 regulates the rabies virus phosphoprotein stability by targeting to Hsp90AA1 machinery.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AA1/Hsp90alpha; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Rabies virus infection and viral P-protein expression in N2a/HEK293T cell systems with CDC37/Hsp90 perturbation.
evidence_limitations: The validated substrate is viral P protein; CDC37 should not be interpreted as an HSP90 client.
claim_summary: CDC37 and HSP90AA1/Hsp90 chaperone the rabies virus P protein: inhibition/knockdown destabilizes P, overexpression maintains stability, and co-IP/truncation experiments support CDC37/Hsp90 machinery involvement. This is CDC37 cochaperone/chaperone-cycle evidence, not CDC37 client evidence.

source.title: Interaction of heat-shock protein 90 beta isoform (HSP90 beta) with cellular inhibitor of apoptosis 1 (c-IAP1) is required for cell differentiation.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90AB1/Hsp90beta; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Human THP1 monocytic differentiation, primary monocyte/macrophage differentiation, and HT-29 sodium-butyrate epithelial differentiation models.
evidence_limitations: No purified binary binding experiment; inhibitor experiments are pan-HSP90/compound-context. The strongest isoform specificity comes from HSP90alpha versus HSP90beta IP/siRNA comparisons.
claim_summary: The full-text source supports c-IAP1/BIRC2 as an HSP90beta/HSP90AB1 client-like stability substrate: c-IAP1 IP/MS detected HSP90beta peptides, HSP90beta co-IP and FRET support association, HSP90alpha was a weak/negative comparator, HSP90 inhibitors and HSP90beta-specific siRNA reduce c-IAP1, and MG132/ubiquitination/RING-domain data support proteasome-linked auto-ubiquitination after HSP90 loss.

source.title: The mitochondrial chaperone TRAP1 promotes neoplastic growth by inhibiting succinate dehydrogenase.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves TRAP1; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: SAOS-2, HCT116, HeLa, RWPE, MEF, and human colorectal cancer mitochondrial/respiration models.
evidence_limitations: The paper demonstrates TRAP1-SDHA/SDH association and enzymatic inhibition, but not purified binary binding or canonical folding/maturation/stability client biology for SDHA.
claim_summary: Primary full text supports TRAP1-resolved SDHA/SDH complex direct activity regulation: BN-PAGE places TRAP1 with complex II/SDH, reciprocal TRAP1-SDHA co-IP is reported, mitochondrial crosslinking plus TRAP1 IP detects SDHA, and TRAP1 knockdown/rescue or 17-AAG changes complex II/SQR activity.

source.title: The mitochondrial chaperone TRAP1 promotes neoplastic growth by inhibiting succinate dehydrogenase.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves TRAP1; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: SAOS-2, HCT116, HeLa, RWPE, MEF, and human colorectal cancer mitochondrial/respiration models.
evidence_limitations: This source names SDHA in the direct co-IP/crosslinking readouts. SDHB remains complex-II support from this paper; separate reviewed rows already cover TRAP1-SDHB interaction/stability from later primary sources.
claim_summary: Primary full text supports SDHB as part of the inspected SDH/complex II context: Figure 3 uses SDHB in BN-PAGE/SDS-PAGE detection of complex II, while the strongest named co-IP/crosslinking readout is SDHA. SDHB is therefore retained as SDH-complex support, not as a direct TRAP1-SDHB binding claim from this paper.

source.title: AI662270/GRP94 axis couples the unfolded protein response to mitochondrial dynamics during acute myocardial infarction.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90B1/GRP94; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Mouse acute myocardial infarction and hypoxic/tunicamycin-treated cardiomyocyte GRP94/ANXA2/AKT1/OPA1 experiments.
evidence_limitations: Strong GRP94-Anxa2 interaction and functional regulation in hypoxic cardiomyocytes, but not purified binary binding or classical folding/maturation client evidence.
claim_summary: Primary full text reports GRP94 co-IP/LC-MS/MS interactome profiling in hypoxia/TN-treated cardiomyocytes, identifies Anxa2 as the top hypoxia GRP94 interactor, confirms mutual GRP94-Anxa2 co-IP, and shows Anxa2 knockdown blocks GRP94-driven p-Akt1 elevation, L-Opa1 generation, mitochondrial protection, and antiapoptotic effects.

source.title: AI662270/GRP94 axis couples the unfolded protein response to mitochondrial dynamics during acute myocardial infarction.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves HSP90B1/GRP94; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Mouse acute myocardial infarction and hypoxic/tunicamycin-treated cardiomyocyte GRP94/ANXA2/AKT1/OPA1 experiments.
evidence_limitations: No GRP94-OPA1 direct interaction is shown; OPA1 is retained only as a downstream functional context for the GRP94-Anxa2-Akt1 axis.
claim_summary: The source shows GRP94 and ANXA2 regulate Opa1 proteolytic processing and L-Opa1 abundance during hypoxic cardiomyocyte stress; OPA1 is the downstream mitochondrial-dynamics output rather than a GRP94 binding partner.

source.title: Profibrotic IHG-1 complexes with renal disease associated HSPA5 and TRAP1 in mitochondria.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves TRAP1; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Tagged IHG-1/THG1L interaction screening, endogenous kidney-cell co-IP, diabetic nephropathy/CKD expression datasets, and mouse UUO renal fibrosis protein time course.
evidence_limitations: HSPA5 support is mediated through an IHG-1/THG1L-centered complex; the source does not establish HSPA5 as a TRAP1 client, a direct TRAP1 binder, or a general mitochondrial HSPA5 mechanism.
claim_summary: HSPA5 appears as an IHG-1/THG1L-associated protein by IP/MS, validates as an IHG-1-V5 co-IP partner, and is found with endogenous IHG-1 in a complex that also contains TRAP1 in kidney cells. The paper frames HSPA5 as renal-disease-associated stress/UPR support in an IHG-1 mitochondrial complex, not as a direct TRAP1-HSPA5 binary interaction.

source.title: Profibrotic IHG-1 complexes with renal disease associated HSPA5 and TRAP1 in mitochondria.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves TRAP1; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: HeLa/HEK293 tagged IHG-1 and delta-mitochondrial-targeting-sequence constructs, kidney-cell endogenous co-IP, diabetic nephropathy/CKD expression datasets, and mouse UUO renal fibrosis protein time course.
evidence_limitations: The gene is discussed in the article as IHG-1; official human symbol is THG1L. Evidence supports an endogenous mitochondrial complex with TRAP1, not purified binary THG1L-TRAP1 binding or a TRAP1 client relationship.
claim_summary: The primary article identifies IHG-1/THG1L-associated proteins by V5 immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometry, lists TRAP1 among selected binding proteins, validates endogenous IHG-1 in a complex with TRAP1 and HSPA5 by co-IP in kidney cells, and reports inverse TRAP1 protein changes in renal fibrosis models where IHG-1 increases.

source.title: Interplay between TRAP1 and Sirtuin-3 Modulates Mitochondrial Respiration and Oxidative Stress to Maintain Stemness of Glioma Stem Cells.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves TRAP1; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: Glioma stem cell models X01 and 528NS, differentiated counterparts, mitochondrial extracts, gamitrinib, TRAP1/SIRT3 siRNA or overexpression, SIRT3 activity, ROS, OCR, ETC subunits, xenograft tumor assays.
evidence_limitations: Strong TRAP1-resolved chaperone/activity evidence, but the relationship remains context-specific and not yet generalized as a final canonical TRAP1 client call across tissues.
claim_summary: User-retrieved primary article and supplement support SIRT3 as a TRAP1-associated mitochondrial chaperone/regulatory target in glioma stem cells: GST-TRAP1 pulldown captures labeled SIRT3, reciprocal mitochondrial IP detects TRAP1/SIRT3 association, TRAP1 siRNA or gamitrinib reduces SIRT3 abundance/activity, TRAP1 activates SIRT3 in vitro, and SIRT3 deacetylates TRAP1 while both regulate ETC complex stability and respiration.

source.title: The mitochondrial chaperone protein TRAP1 mitigates alpha-Synuclein toxicity.

isoform_scope_note: The source resolves TRAP1; exclusivity relative to other isoforms is not inferred.
model_context: A53T alpha-synuclein Drosophila dopaminergic-neuron model, rat primary cortical neurons, HEK293 and SH-SY5Y cell assays, oxidative stress, complex I activity, and mitochondrial morphology.
evidence_limitations: Evidence supports TRAP1 mitigation of mutant alpha-synuclein toxicity and mitochondrial dysfunction, but not direct binding, folding/maturation of SNCA, or a canonical client call.
claim_summary: Primary source evidence shows TRAP1 modifies mutant alpha-synuclein toxicity: reduced TRAP1 enhances A53T alpha-synuclein dopamine/neuron loss, locomotor decline, and oxidative-stress sensitivity in fly models, while human TRAP1 overexpression rescues fly, rat primary-neuron, and human-cell stress/mitochondrial phenotypes including complex I activity and mitochondrial morphology. This supports TRAP1-resolved functional protection downstream of SNCA toxicity, not direct SNCA-TRAP1 binding or SNCA client maturation.

source.title: Hepatic lipase maturation: a partial proteome of interacting factors.

source.title: Apoprotein B degradation is promoted by the molecular chaperones hsp90 and hsp70.

isoform_scope_note: The source does not resolve cytosolic Hsp90alpha from Hsp90beta; no isoform specificity is inferred.
